title: The Folly of Human Riches
english: Our best prophets, the helpless animals, the simple images of God, and the faithful slaves of our life in freedom are filled with insolence. Thus the perfect, the poor, the children, and the rustic ones [are affected]. Some toil, some grumble, and some learn what is not good to know.

Let us consider how even unarmed soldiers are harmed by this festival. They suffer financial loss and, for a single lapse, they offer the food-allowance of war. They are harmed in their ways and characters. For they learn lawlessness, the conveniences of tents, and a dissolution and softness of character, and childishness against the laws and the order for which they were set as guards.

For they mock and drag down the greatest authority, ascending like a chariot upon a stage, and ordaining spear-bearers with minds gone astray, and publicly doing things of the outcasts toward ruin. And these are the most solemn things of the procession. And as for the others, how could anyone say?

Does not even the hero, he who is lion-hearted, who after being armed was seen as wonderful by his own people and fearsome to his enemies, also become womanish when having uncovered himself? And he lets the tunic go down to the hips, and wraps the belt around his chest, and uses womanish sandals, and places the fillet upon his head, which is a law for women? And he carries the wool-filled basket and lowers the thread with his right hand, which once used to carry the trophy? And alternating the tone of the soul, does he speak more sharply and womanishly? These are the useful things of the festival; the...

These are the things concerning the public feast today. And those having ascended to the summit of human offices, the much-boasting officials, spend their wealth in vanity, scattering heaps of money toward the unfruitfulness of justice and the fruit of sin; of which the folly is so conspicuous, as high as the throne.

For having entered into many human thrones and having governed the greatest of royal authorities, they take ungraciously the greatest things from everything; some having embezzled the rations of poor soldiers, others many times having sold justice and truth, and others having exhausted the wealth of the royal treasuries without limit and having diligently gathered from everywhere; yet being sparing of no reproach, not being lacking, not being unjust; and provoking God, they sit now, and after a little time dividing the gold to vagabonds, ill-fated ones, and mimes and dancers and androgynes and women who are prostitutes, providing the body to the people; and again to impure and hopeless gladiators and to the beasts themselves. For it is evident, just as gold feeds the beasts, one buying meat for them, another the fodder.

And all these things are prepared with one haste, so that the names of their transactions may be written beforehand. Oh, the madness! Oh, the blindness! God promises to write the names of the nurturers of the poor in living books, the immortal ones, the incorruptible ones, which you do not make vanish and time does not erase; and those letters you will not see, nor will you make any account.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Vanity of Earthly Riches and Honors
english: Do you not seek to be written in the memory of God, rather than in the promise of blessedness? For this is the living book.

He speaks much of writing by contract-writers, and of the uneducated speaking crudely and making noise, and of flatterers among the people; a bad judge of the need of things, and a thoughtless examiner of what is profitable.

Give to the impoverished man who is struggling, not to the ruined musician; grant to the widow before the prostitute, and to the venerable woman who has been called forth before the public. Labor for the orphan, whom a holy virgin sings to God, and not for a shameless singer who cares only for the sight of the crowd to hunt for followers; satisfy the orphan, release the debt of the poor, and you shall see a glory that endures forever.

Many purses are cast into emptiness for the sake of shameful and disorderly laughter, not knowing how many tears the poor bestow, from which abundance was gathered; how many were bound, how many were flogged, how many came near the yoke and the bridle, so that today those who are indulging may receive. And what is the end? Vanity.

After everything, a small tomb, the body shrinking to a garment of a few obols, oblivion after a little while, and the consuming passion of time covering all that was labored for; judgment upon these is inevitable, from God and the punishment of evil disposition.

Where are the governors? Count those of yesterday and of former times. One was not cut off like the criminals of the head, falling through the continuous movement of a charging multitude; and was he sent off more like a funeral than when he was being carried upon a litter in the pride of his office? Another, having attained honor through the same military strategy, perished badly in the outskirts of Egypt and Libya, fleeing the punishment of the sentence, and finally entreating the sands, since all the land through which he wandered was waterless and uninhabited.
And what shall we say of the one from among the generals and governors, who is now passing through the land of Colchis and is being saved by the philanthropy of the barbarians there?

And that one from the former times, who, as he thought, had a fearless and lion-like mind—what a destruction of life he endured! First, he saw his own son being decapitated; then he himself received the vote for death, and when the rope was already being brought to his mouth, a royal philanthropy restrained the executioner from acting. Having lived a little longer, the old man delayed his end through pains and misfortunes and through the perception of evils, departing from life in disgrace, finding this to be the end of great governorship.

And how he of the past year cared for greater things than the giants, being able to contend with both women and men; fleeing the rods of lords, he desired the rods of governors; he acquired land such that it is not easy even to say, yet he was buried in as much as the one who pitied him bestowed.

Is it not, then, according to the wise Ecclesiastes (Eccl 1:2), that all such things are vanity of vanities, and honors are phantoms of unsubstantial dreams, pleasing for a little while, then passing away, blooming and then withering? We, therefore, standing firm in the Word until then, let us send glory to the Savior.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Purpose of Marriage and the Women's Question
english: This is the same homily of Asterius from the Gospel according to Matthew, on the subject: 'Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any cause?'

A good company of these two days is found for the Christians and the hard-working ones, I say, the Sabbath and the Lord's Day, which the cycle of time revolves around every week. For just as mothers or nurses of the church gather the people and establish the priests as teachers, they also lead the disciples and the teachers into the care of souls. For me, therefore, the word of the Friday still echoes, and the things suffered are settled in the memory.

I see the cross springing from the prophecy of Isaiah, and the garments of the Lord as if stained with blood like those of the lamb, and the Savior carrying the reward at hand on his right hand. And I see Solomon, the scales and the weights being precise for power. And I pity the debtor of the Gospel, not sharing with the fellow-slave of philanthropy, which he received from the master, but renewing his own misfortune from thoughtlessness and hardness of heart.
For these headings, as you all know, we burned with desire during the past [session], you who did not place your listening in a secondary matter.

But today again there are many and all good things for us, as many as the Spirit has set upon the table being seen. And I applied my mind to the unhospitable and testing Pharisees, and I pitied them greatly for the exhaustion of their ways, through which they attempted to appear wise by their own questions, seeking the source of wisdom; and they failed to grasp the essence of the Only-begotten Divinity, as their questions were always turning away from it.
Concerning these, it seems to me, Isaiah also, prophesying, was saying: 'They turn the prudent backward and make foolish their counsel, and they weave the words of his child'; and again...

They were acting deceitfully with their tongues; let God judge them; let them fall away from their conspiracies. However, they are even useful, for they have set wisdom in motion toward an answer, so that for us, the servants, a record remains of what is profitable for learning.

For behold, marriage is being regulated, a central matter of human life, and the terms for its joining and its dissolving are being strictly legislated. Let the two ranks listen most earnestly, so that the women's sphere may be instructed in its own matters and the men's sphere may be benefited by the exceptional things.

If it is permitted for a man to divorce his wife for every cause (Matt 19:3)—this is the question posed by the Hebrews. I see the purpose of the question among the others. Because the female race is more easily persuaded and leans more toward the working of wonders and toward the agreement and faith in the divinity of Christ, even so, the multitude of women, who were the last of the man-slayers by drawing the Lord toward the cross by their will, were moved to passion and followed the Savior weeping compassionately, so that they might devise some obstacle and hostility toward Him through the mechanism of women's schemes—they themselves, as they thought, applied the traps and the yokes through words.

But the Lord, seeing the wickedness being constructed by the power of divinity, and also dogmatizing the friends of the cross in their lives, working for them a vain ambush, while assisting the women, puts forward the answer, having sent the Pharisees away empty like wolves, surrounding them with the hollow question. She [Creation] says, the purpose is demonstrated for union and not for dissolution; and regarding marriage, the Creator was first the wedding-procession leader, having joined the first-formed men in the bond of marriage, giving to them...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Role and Fidelity of the Wife
english: After being born, the sequence of living together is necessary, which should be honored as God's law. Those joined to one another are no longer two, but one flesh; so what God has joined, let no man separate (Matthew 19:6). These things were said to the Pharisees then; but now listen, you who easily change markets and wives like garments; who frequently and easily frequent the brothels as if they were festival works; who marry for ease and trade wives; who are easily provoked and immediately write the document of divorce; who leave many widows while still living.

Be persuaded that marriage is cut off only by death and adultery. For it is not like the concubines, where a short number of days disturbs the living together and only hunts pleasure, so it is with those performed according to law and decree; but on the contrary, O man, a single union occurs of both body and soul, just as character is intertwined with character and the flesh is in a certain way bound to the flesh.

How then will you cut it off indifferently? How will you easily and without pain withdraw, having taken a share of life, having served for only a few days, the sister and wife? A sister according to the word of formation and creation, for from one cause of the earth and the same matter you came into being; but a wife through the union of the marriage, through the law of marriage.

What then bond will you break, being bound by law and by nature? And how will you set aside the vows which you laid upon the marriage? And who does he think I am to speak to you? Is it perhaps regarding the dowry written here, when with your own hand I mark it in the book while sealing the completed things?
For those are indeed strong and have sufficient security; yet I refer myself to the voice of Adam (Genesis 2:23): 'This is flesh of my flesh and bone of my bones; she shall be called my wife.'

This voice is not preserved as a vain copy, but is a common confession of men, set forth through the one person of this first man for the common multitude of women joining to men by law. And do not marvel if, from those whom another said, another is held accountable. For all things that happened concerning the first-formed in the beginning, these...

A nature of a following kind was produced. If, having taken the book of creation, a wife abandoned her mother and dragged you before the judge, the very same judge and witness, what words would you say? How will you erase your own voice, which you made before God, where the writer became Moses, the servant of God, instead of a mere scribe?

God gave the woman to Adam without fault and without blemish, and for this reason, as a good guardian, He protected the orphan. But now daughters use the rights of the mother strongly against ignorant and faithless men, so that for you, contempt for the wife is impossible from any direction, being bound by the ancient divine laws and the new human ones.

Let the usefulness of the woman for life also restrain you. She is a member, she is a helper; a partner for the enjoyment of life and for the generation of children; a helper in sickness, a consolation in tribulations, a guardian of the hearth, a treasure of possessions; the same when grieving, the same when rejoicing; possessing wealth in common, if it should fail; managing hard poverty, bravely and patiently enduring what is painful through her, toiling in child-rearing because of her dwelling with you.

But if a crisis of circumstances should seize her, she vanishes when baptized; but those considered friends, measuring friendship by the season of prosperity, withdraw in terrible times; slaves flee both the master and the misfortunes together.

Therefore, the wife remains: a member of the part that is sick, a slave to the evils, and the tear that wipes away the healing of the husband; healing the wound if it is struck; following the one being led to prison; and even if one allows her to enter, she shares the pleasure of the confinement; but if even this is forbidden, she remains at the doors of the prison, as a little dog accustomed to her master.

I knew a woman who had cut her hair and put on manly clothing, this flowering garment, so that she would not be separated while the man was fleeing and hiding. She seemed to be a slave, but truly she was a slave to passion; and she lived this life for many years, moving from place to place and from desert to desert. We find such a thing also in the most patient Job.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Virtues of a Wife vs. the Cruelty of Men
english: For everyone left her; even the flatterers fled with the wealth, and friends measured their friendship by the season of prosperity. If they did happen to appear, their presence was a reproach rather than a visit; a burden of misfortune, not a consolation. Therefore, all the bad comforters withdrew from him.

But she, who was once distinguished by her toil, stayed with her husband, leaving aside the filth and pulling out the worms of the wounds. Thus, she was a partner of his life, not a companion of his prosperity; an inseparable friend, not a flatterer of pleasures; leaving behind only all kindness, all most-dear qualities, and all kinship.

Therefore, out of extreme and excessive friendship for a man, and toward the sin of blasphemy, she fell, so that the man might not be punished for a long time, nor see him in unmanageable pains, by saying a blasphemous word toward God, advising [him] and that he might undergo a swift end. For she did not consider her own remaining misfortune, that of widowhood; but she had only one concern, how the man might escape an unlivable life. These things, along with the new trial and the memory of the old, instruct the wedding-insulter.

What then would the one responsible for the accusation say toward these things? And what kind of fair-faced defense of his own ease would he put forward? 'Worthless,' he says, 'and worthy of hatred is the character of the woman, and her tongue is impudent, and her manner is not domestic, and her management is lawless.' Let it be so; let it be granted. I am completely persuaded and I accept, that judges who are not very precise in hearing easily are dragged along by the attacks of the accusers.

But you say: 'While leading the beginning, did you not know that you were connecting with a human? And having heard of a human, does one not immediately see a small sin following? For God's alone is the ungraspable. Do you not yourself sin? And do you not cause grief to the woman by your manner? And are you innocent of all wrongdoing and do you keep the institution of living together without corruption?'

O how much chance of rebuke your wife brought! And how many ready insults and indecent words she endured! And how many of your faults are kept silent, because the woman did not publish them! She endured you even while you were becoming angry and your spirit was boiling; and the free and equal [one] was silenced.

She was like a slave from a market. She did not reproach you for not providing the necessities for the conduct of life due to poverty or stinginess. Nor did she ever reject you after coming from a banquet, having drunk wine and being out of her mind because she hated drunkenness; rather, she received you with human sympathy, and she led you, who were punishing yourself, and she treated the head with the vapors of the wine being poured out. And she alone, sympathizing, led you to the marriage bed, while the servants were laughing and mocking the excess from the drunkenness.

But you, bypassing the amphorae, sing songs against the woman on cold pretexts, so that you might prepare sympathy for yourself for the imminent division. The mind of such men is hard, beastly and unmerciful, having a birth from oak or stone, according to what is said. For they are cut off indifferently, erasing the memory of all at once.

But who, instead of healing a sick limb, cuts it off, and this not having considered a dangerous disease, but having much hope for an easy cure? A blister occurred on the hand, let us treat it carefully; an inflammation pursued the foot, let us settle the irritation with medicine. And if, being present, we had attended to the physicians' inspection regarding the incision and the iron, and had occupied ourselves with each of those who were suffering, we would not have lost even a small amount of life's time, but would have amputated ourselves for all the limbs.

But not so, O men; let there be some memory of the punishments; let the healings of women make you ashamed. However much you may be provoked, if you withstand the pangs of a single birth against the reproaches, you will find the situation of those who suffer to be conquered.

Let the calculation be referred to the middle, and let the good things be included in the goodwill: the healing of diseases, the sharing of misfortunes, the tears presented to some on behalf of a husband, the leaving of those she gave birth to and the parental table to follow a stranger, the selling of something of her own so that she might drive away the insolence and trouble of the husband. Let all these things instruct toward a disposition and let them become a bond of affection, such as a more modest house awakening and holding together the easily slipping soul. But let mercy prevail, and habit, and living together for a long time, let it not be struck by...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Bond of Marriage and the Call to Sobriety
english: It is irrational of animals to be held together without passion. For I saw with passion a bellowing ox, because having wandered from its companions it remained stuck, and a sheep being thrown into a pit and running through the mountains until it could reunite with the flock from which it was separated while grazing. And a goat, experiencing this same thing, even if it runs through many herds of kids, does not stand still until it finds its usual place and its own sharp-edged way.

Therefore, let us not be found more passionless toward friendship than the irrational ones who are rational, nor let us judge the marriage of a companion to be less honorable because of having become friendly in a short time through a small pretext. You see how even on the high road, men having mixed with one another, having gone under the same roof of a building or having shaded themselves at midday in a tree embracing them in the season of summer, make the encounter an occasion for genuine disposition; and even if they come to the road that divides, they do not depart from one another passionlessly, but they stand and weep, looking intently at one another, and each gives tokens of memory to carry; and having advanced a little, they turn back again and call out, and one prays for the other the spiritual things; and does a little time thus sharpen the friendship so acutely, that it becomes unchangeable to them and their departure is established?

But you, toward the one who is a sharer of life, act so contemptuously, as toward a vessel fallen or a cheap garment forgotten on a journey or a rag of the Melitians departing a house? And where is the disposition formed in the beginning? Where is the rest upon the one bed, the joining of the law, the strength of much and long habit, which is even transformed into nature and has a reason, and experience has shown? Having cut off everything more easily than Samson cut the cords of the Philistines (Judges 16).

Even if he is sober and a guardian of his disposition, he does not easily forget the life of the marriage even after it has departed, but he warms the children as a common deposit of the mother and of nature, and in them he seems to see the one who has gone. For one preserves the likeness of the mother's voice, another is drawn to much of the character, another is formed in the state of the character toward the one who bore him; and thus the father [preserves] many.

Having the living and manifest image of the marriage as an immortal pattern, he imagines the cohabitation toward it and for this reason does not conceive any unseemly thought. Not today, having entered the tomb, after a little time, does he prepare wedding feasts; nor does he hasten to a wedding dance again after the weeping and the groans; nor does he mix the black and mourning garment into a bridal attire; nor does he introduce a second marriage into the warm bed of the one who has departed; nor does he give the heavy name to the children.

He imitates the irrational and natural dignity of the birds. For they say that even that bird, having been separated from its mate, loves the widowship continuously and stands in opposition to the dove, making it easy toward polygamy.

Until this, let the man be cast heavily with accusations, and let the insults of ignorance sting him more densely with veils. If, however, an accusation of adultery is brought forward and such is provided as the defense for the separation, I will immediately shift my sympathy to the wronged one, and having prepared the argument against the adulteress, I will stand as a good ally to the man instead of an enemy, praising the one who fled the aggressor, the one who broke the bond to which he was bound with a shield or an echidna.

For by this, the Creator of all gives forgiveness first, as it is just for one who is suffering and rightly driving away the sickness of the house and the hearth. For marriage consists of these two: disposition and child-rearing, neither of which is saved after adultery. For the disposition is not one that turns away from another of goodwill; and child-rearing is lost when the children are poured out.

But regarding those leading toward this, the sin is stated in another hypothesis proportionately. Let both sides practice sobriety, the unbreakable bond of marriages. For where this is honored, there must always be both peace and longing, without the soul desiring any common and illegitimate passion, casting out the lawful and just affection.
This law of sobriety was established by God not for women only, but also for men. And those paying attention to the law-makers of this life are not without shame.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Overflowing Grace of the Spirit
english: Men leave the power of fornication to themselves; they are heavy judges and teachers of women's modesty, while they themselves trespass upon many bodies, being like doctors who, according to the proverb, infect with a myriad of lures.

Even if one of them falls into these transgressions, they present a decorated and playful defense. For men say that even if they approach many women, they do not defile their own hearth; but women, from whom they sin, introduce alien heirs to the houses and the lineages. Let the sophists and finders of the adulterous opinion listen, that they themselves also overturn other hearths and houses.

For the women with whom they associate are certainly either daughters or wives of someone; and in every way, either a marriage is being plotted against or a parent is being wronged, he who fathered and reared and hoped to have a virgin upon the paving and in the bridal chamber, but all good expectation was taken away from him by the robbers of temperance.

If the dissolute man is a father, let him recognize the father's suffering being missed; if a husband, let him represent himself as the one being wronged. For it is easy thus to judge others for everyone, as if he would wish another for himself. If some, paying attention to certain Roman laws, unashamedly consider fornication to be permissible, they are terribly wandering in error, not knowing that God legislates differently and men dogmatize differently.

Listen to Moses announcing the will of God and bringing forth the bitter decisions concerning fornicators. Listen to Paul saying: 'God will judge fornicators and adulterers' (1 Cor 6:9). And the others will not suffice you for salvation at the time of retribution, but trembling and sweating, they will be consumed. To you, Plato, the sophist of laws, will appear foolish and uneducated, and that heavy tone will be humbled, having had its power lifted against all lawgivers.
When they see the bodily ones being dragged away, to whom they themselves have badly affected the authority.

But certainly those not having prevented others, they first turned the sin toward themselves and will be found guilty of a double charge, which they themselves practiced and for which they left others to live without restraint. Therefore, those wishing to live with the worldly as if with most precious brides, let them themselves make their own way a teacher of their housemates, so that they may have good zeal from the hearth.

Word of Asterius Bishop of Amaseia on the prophet Daniel and on Susanna. Always having the grace of the Spirit overflowing, the wealth of the gift does not fail its own supply nor those whom it wishes to demonstrate. For just as a river, filled with waters leaping toward life, stands opposite to those seeing this and according to the earth, it has the releases of its energies being granted.

For the stream does not fail it just as for those sometimes, nor does it receive rises and falls as they do, nor does it contain both the whole and the part according to these, but it fills always and suffices for all; and flowing toward the partakers of the fullness, it remains nothing less than full, for indeed having the grace thus abundant, it knows not how to distribute and divide even according to ages.

For the immeasurable things do not know how to be measured by the bulk of bodies, but by the nobility and purity of soul to come together and to shine forth. And because of this, now it behaves toward Samuel being nourished with milk, but now it takes up David from his sheep, rising above the brothers to whom it seemed to overlook him because of the incompleteness of his age.

Another, perfected by the anointing from a different source, and with those now lying in hypothesis, the blessed and truly wise Daniel, still soft and at the same time fresh in harvest, establishes as judge and prophet both of the young and the elders; who, even if the heavy work of that captivity has become his, and
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Exhortation to Moral Renewal
english: The Babylon captivity had taken hold, and through the passage of time, the incomplete and without confidence appeared in dishonor because of being seized by so many evils. But from the bringing forth of virtue and being instructed in philosophy, the first growth and being steadfast and deep in mind, in that very flower of the age, the control and judge of those elders was being shown. But let us see, if it seems to you, by bringing the word back to the beginning, how to be a friend to God is lofty and blessed.

When the city of Jerusalem was taken by war from the Assyrians, the peoples of the Hebrews then were dispersed to Babylon. And there was also the blessed Daniel, a multitude of spear-wielding youths, and a cheerful boy was recounting the war, a small and much-suffering people, having neither an occasion from his kinsmen to appear, nor being considered a worthy gain of war by the enemies; invisible, without glory because of age and because of misfortune; seen only by the one looking well.

For God alone saw the pure soul of the youth, just as a pearl enveloped in shell-like oysters or gold lying in the hollows of the earth; as a bride properly covered with the veils of the dais. And when the appointed time came and it was necessary for the hidden to be revealed, for the invisible to become known, for the despised to be looked upon, for the one hidden by the darkness of misfortune to shine, a little effusion of the Spirit, and the humble of all to be higher; wise he who does not divide the mouth; a judge of hidden things; a critic of judges; sitting on a high throne, having not yet become a servant of courts; the young man avenging temperance being slandered, turning back a wandering people, calling back the vote of the whole city having been wrongly cast.
Listen...

Therefore, hold fast your soul to the reading and to the wonder in every way. And I, having left aside the matters of other books, which the psalms have profitably sung to us with pleasure, which the apostle advised, and which the Lord has masterfully legislated in the gospels, have been drawn to this history.
For I see two youths of excellence: one in the act of judging, and the other in the act of being judged; and Daniel being struck with votes, and Susanna being crowned with the victory of temperance.

Come then, if it seems good, you lovers of beautiful things and of virtue, let us renew the ancient judgment by memory; let us cut away the present lawlessness with ancient temperance, having stepped in as elders, admiring a maidenhood that has become old and a youth that has become urbanized. O defiled elders and leaders of the people, who desire to join those joined by the law of marriage, needing ten thousand teachers for restoration, lurking in temperance, schemers of deceits, quick finders of slander!

You were the ones judging fornication with your lips and condemning adultery; being doctors of others and becoming the disease themselves; being tombs struck full within of uncleanness and beautifying the outward appearance. The high ones, sitting upon the thrones of judges, when you invited lawlessness by creeping into the thickets of plants and shrubs.

Then the accuser of transgressions and the counselor of evils laughed seeing you, how those at the top of the people, the eloquent and the chosen, have drawn near to the land like certain wall-burrowers or robbers, in order to behold an uncontrolled spectacle; and you hid yourselves in the shrubs according to the thickets, which from the tangled and shady places house the birds and unexpectedly leap upon the dwellers.
O, what a similar evil, which the destroyer of human souls from the beginning unto...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Corruption of the Court and the Appeal to God
english: The end is fitting! In Paradise, the first fall of the exalted man occurred; in Paradise also now the elders, being worked by the serpent, fall away from the original glory, becoming condemned instead of judges, workers not of life but of sin.

But there, the man prevailed, while the woman was defeated, and the emptiness of the first woman found no maiden upon the Babylonian. And one could rightly say that Babylon is not a confusion because of Susanna, but a keeping of God's commandments, a guard of temperance, a city of a manly woman, a place of a triumphal feast.

This I, having ascended through the middle times, lead to Joseph by the likeness of virtue toward the world; but I set the honorable woman beside the temperate one who is a friend of God, beside the child of Israel. I place one and the same crown upon both, the one for temperance; and I cast down the defeated ones beneath the feet of the victors: to Joseph, the unrestrained Egypt, the mistress of the free slave; but to Susanna, the dishonorable elders.

I set these as teachers of temperance: the one of womanhood, the other of the youth of men; lamps of the inhabited world, flowers of the resurrection, judges of adultery, guardians of lawful marriages. Finally, let us occupy ourselves only with the sacred woman's account; for now Joseph is an episode and the temperate one is a parenthesis of temperance.

Because the elders, as they thought, had the hunt within nets, and stepped out from the thicket to take prey immediately, they did not find the most cowardly deer, but one standing against them both and against the dragon who is the cause of these things, but a deer-slayer animal; and the account rightly found the image of the animal: they enticed, but were not heard; they threatened, but did not strike terror.
Therefore the wicked are helpless and are held by two great things...

By chance of desire and fear of rebuke. But filthy sums of money seize slander, and for a solution to evil they find another evil, and they prepare a cover for adultery through murder. For a sinner, when he falls into the beginnings of transgressions, like a splinter at the start, he drags along the following lawlessness. And he happens to beget of the good things the good, and of the bad things the similar.

Therefore also now murder is the fruit of adultery, and a council sits in haste as if upon a great injustice against the woman, and a crowd is led away having the one being judged as a spectacle. And the accusers and the judges are the same; and many a slandering person was deemed trustworthy, and a youth being slandered was condemned from the prevailing suspicion.

And a people, being tossed about and suffering—for a people is accustomed to be struck by impulse—was driven astray in indignation and was carried along by the impulse of the elders; the parents of the one being judged wailed, the husband suffered the calamity, the children wailed from here and there, being distraught because of the mother's danger, and the race was covered by shame.

But the good judges, the fellow-combatants of temperance, commanded her, having her dignity solemnly covered by a garment—for she, possessing decorum, had rushed to be naked—not even regarding the confusion of evils, so that in the court of adultery, they might perform adultery against the adultery, giving rest to the shameful desire by the sight of the one being judged. And they placed hands upon the head, which was a symbol of condemnation, using a clean body; the unrestrained ones, through touch and through it, were proselytizing the lie, while the good ones are defenders of the truth.

And as the people were subdued and the vote was cast and the punishment was near, the one being slandered then looked up to the judge of judges; she brought the legal case from men to God, making an appeal to the Unaccountable.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Judgment and the Pattern of Holiness
english: A courtroom, and the truth was not delayed.

Therefore, arise to me, O blessed Daniel, and now by the word as you were awakened, and then by the Spirit; say also that you are innocent of this blood, just as Pilate later [did] against the raving Hebrews. Analyze the people upon the criterion; give a beginning to the justice that has been badly completed; set the false judges to be judged; let the order of the protectors be changed, and let the woman observe the elders, just as she herself a little while ago was a spectacle of the city.

Let the captive judge the citizens; the stranger the locals; the youth the old. Use a holy mouth for the Spirit; for you do not have unclean lips, as Isaiah says of himself reviling himself; nor do you need one of the Seraphim or the cleansing coal. Depart wisely from the false judges, so that they may not also leap upon your own questions as a woman [leaps] in paradise.

For how we may clearly learn the beginning of the words of the thrice-blessed child: Having grown old through days of evil, now your sins, which you did formerly, have come to you, condemning the innocent and releasing the guilty. O the wonder and the great liberty of the Spirit! For where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.

See, for it does not even hold back in the preambles; but, piercing into the depth of the conscience and seeing the souls of the elders as storehouses of sins, it seeks neither witness nor proofs; but is insulted and reviled with insolence, because the prophet has the decision written upon his chest.

And as far as it reached him, he would not even have said anything, but he sent them away unreservedly to the punishment; so that he might convince a foolish people and empty judges of the city, who accuse but do not judge according to the truth, and he brings to them the experience of questioning, separated from the truth and the falsehood of the [discourse]...

Mindful of the response, he exposes; and having brought forth the judgment, he does not give accountability to humans, but calls angels to be tormentors against them. For the dignity of the saints has grown to such an extent that they have invisible powers serving them.

What then happens to the defiled? Judgment was prepared; and they went away, giving the penalty through death for the old lawlessness and the new sin; and all Babylon had the paradox of what was happening through the mouth, and they blasphemed God with hymns, having made public the knowledge of the hidden deeds. And Hezekiah was refreshed rejoicing over the daughter; Joachim made a triumph for the feast of the wife; and twenty-nine children, legitimate and of temperate offspring, smile with faces surrounding the mother, and the much-teared grief was transformed into joy.

You, however, the people of Christ, most pious and soul-benefiting, having heard these histories, do not let the hearing pass by indifferently, but make the word a training and discipline for your own life. Women, emulate Susanna; thus guard toward men the temperance as she did toward herself; she accepted to suffer and to be in danger rather than to defile her life with adultery. Adultery provokes God, shames a man, destroys house and hearth, and works uncertain children. You elders, hate such old men; you rulers, fear the end of the lawless judges.

You young people, imitate the young man, so that in this way every age may be formed into the pattern of beautiful character, so that the whole fullness of the church may become holy and well-pleasing in Christ Jesus our Savior, to whom belong glory, might, and honor, with the co-ruling Father and with His all-holy and life-giving Spirit, now and always and unto the ages of ages. Amen.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Master Defends Himself Against Insulters
english: The discourse of Asterius, Bishop of Amaseia, concerning the blind man from the womb. We have recently heard the son of thunder, John, but rather the Holy Spirit working through the fisherman and craftsman, writer and scribe, of truly divine and lofty themes. For he explained to us a great and long discourse of the Lord, through which he instructed the disobedient people and the hard-of-hearing in the knowledge of God, drawing their thoughts away from the monarchical concept of the Hebrews, opening for them the door of grace from the legal tradition, and leading them quietly from the old toward the New Covenant, just as from the desert previously to the rich and fruitful land.

But nevertheless, while he was demonstrating in various ways his own existence, as he exists pre-eternally and is always co-inherent with the Father, and shouting loudly to the deaf: 'Before Abraham was, I am' (John 8:58). Not having learned the power of the Word, nor having examined through any expert opposition that which was not accepted, they were throwing stones instead of words, and from a distance from the cross, they were exercising their murderous hands toward murder. But he who judges everywhere, having long-suffering toward the insulting and blasphemous people, diverted their anger and the noise, not by returning it humbly, but divinely; who, standing in the midst and feeling about, did not see, and being rubbed against by those burning, did not perceive, but they stood near, killing in their will, because of which they would not find the anger to be fulfilled; like inexperienced hunters, who, when they stir up the hunt before the time, and a certain spear of the deer comes running and disappears, they wander aimlessly through the thicket carrying redundant nets and uselessly pulling the dogs.
As for me, even if I am a lowly servant in all other things, I do not depart from this thought, because I am a slave and it is fitting for me on behalf of the...

A master stands up against those who insult him. Therefore I have cried out to the Hebrews who are present today and acting out of madness: 'You wicked ones, are you throwing stones at the benefactor? For who made you out of stone? You throw stones at the one who made your life like flat stones. You throw at the chosen and precious stone which Isaiah foretold to you (Isaiah 28:16). You throw at the intellectual stone, torn from the unhewn rock without human hands, as the divinely inspired Daniel taught you (Daniel 2:34). You throw at the cornerstone which joins the two walls of the new and the old Testament.'

For even if you do not believe, God is able from these stones to raise up children for Abraham, that is, to gather to Christ a remnant people from among the nations and the uncircumcised, upon which Abraham received the promise when God said to him, 'All the nations will be blessed in you' (Genesis 12:3). By secret foreknowledge, seeing the future, God completed the leader of the faith so that all those destined to believe later would be appointed as children in order.

For He was seeing then the stance of the Hebrews and the stones, and He was counting the pseudo-named sons among the outcasts. And since, announcing the truth to them by word, they did not believe in being pious, He stood forth and appeared not to be seen, so that from such a wonder of His He might draw them to an agreement that He indeed was God and was older than Abraham.

'Listen then,' He says, 'O truly blind and senseless ones: Who is this, who is also present with you and is not seen? Or perhaps He is the one who also speaks to Moses and does not appear? For He saw then both fire and the bush, both being silent (Exodus 3). But nonetheless, a voice was heard and a word was instructing and safely foretelling what is to come.' And those having understanding must know the person from the connection of the things.
Thus, irrationally and senseless of the
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Eye as a Masterpiece of Divine Wisdom
english: While the Hebrews had our Lord and Savior, like a careful and wise physician, who does not employ another method of treatment for a first experience of a disease, he intends to heal a blind man who was found from birth, not having become blind through any fault or suffering, but by a defect of nature produced from the womb into life.

Having seen the man, he stood and was ready for healing, a healing superior to human speech and art. For medical speech imposes upon those diseases a theory—those things which, after nature has completed the animal and leads it toward light, happen in certain circumstances later—but when [the disease] is joined to the body, healing is not promised of a fault. Yet not even of all the sufferings that come about later.

And the maimed of men are witnesses to this, for no physician has repaired the loss of their limbs. Therefore also the disciples, having seen the suffering and seeing a man who had not tasted the best pleasure of light, were searching for the cause of the harm and were inquiring from the Lord, not very knowing, whether he was brought into life such as this because of his own sin or because of the faults of his parents (cf. John 9:2).

On both sides the question carries a consequence; for the child would not have been judged on account of the fathers, God not punishing one for another; nor indeed did he escape punishment for his own faults, if this one was born blind. For no one is a sinner before birth. Therefore the inquiry is not very proven; but so that we may learn how the truth, our Lord, responded to the question.

For this suffering, he says, 'O disciples, is not a retribution for sins, but a preparation for an upcoming economy, so that the man formerly considered common might act the things above man, and the Creator of all things, after the first creation, might find an occasion now to create, and through the particular might be made to trust the universal, and the hard and difficult people might be persuaded to worship, casting away the stones.'
Let the eyes that do not see be enlightened, so that the sun of righteousness (cf. Malachi 4:2) might shine upon the souls of the unwise.

Let a paradoxical thing be set forth and new sights be created, so that those who are in dispute may learn how the so-called son of Joseph, if he were truly a carpenter's boy, would have been able to mend a split plank, or gather together wood torn from harmony, or see a broken beam, or smooth the roughness of the boards, or do entirely those things which a craftsman father teaches his son according to the skill of the trade.

And a part of man, and the most beautiful part, the eye, which is most lovingly fashioned by nature, no one else could have made, unless he who has the authority of the first principle according to nature. Even if someone wishes to apply his mind closely to human limbs, in this very thing, the form of the body, he will behold the almighty and manifold wisdom of God in a small descriptive representation, such as the zeal of the art has demonstrated. For first, a certain grace is poured out upon it, and it is both most soft and incorporeal, as one might say, having the solid within the tender, and the arranged within the soft, and it is streaked with various colors.

Its center indeed has the description of black, and this is not a single-colored thing throughout, but connected with various circles; its center and middle having the deepest part, while the outer periphery is fading in color toward the more yellow part. Around this, the white has been draped from without, shining and lucid, not having a white that is unmixed, but having been made in a certain crystalline and beaming form. The red lies around the pupil, so that it may mix grace with the white and the black. Upon these things, it is thus lucid and smooth in its density, so that even those nearby make shapes like images, and like an accurate mirror, the characters of those being conversed with are impressed; for this reason also its middle circle, the center, is called a pupil, always showing a human form to the one looking opposite. For just as it is not possible for one looking into a mirror not to immediately shadow his own character upon the material, so it is not possible for the one standing as a representative of man not to engrave the familiar form upon the eye. When, indeed, men look at one another...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Power of the Siloam Washing
english: They become mirrors to one another. Therefore, the eye is worthy of wonder among the created things. For this also interprets God to me, accurately perceiving all of creation and, by pointing out the artisan through the working of things, it interprets the invisible to the soul from the visible; through this I have knowledge of the sun and the order of the heavens, and I have studied the beauty of the stars and the substance and nature of the earth, the difference of seeds and the variety of plants and the diverse coloring of hues, the depth of darkness and the shining of light, and all simply as much as God has created.

If an eye had not existed, creation would have been without witness, with no one seeing the wisdom and power of God being preserved within it. Because of this, therefore, this wonderful arrangement of the eyes, the eyes were also created by design, so that we might cast off the lowly ideas approaching us from the flesh concerning the Only-begotten, by the great work of things coming to be, casting out from the soul every lowly and vulgar conceit; let us know, however, that the blessed light and beauty of the divinity received an earthen vessel to serve us, like lamps, the shining light.

The Lord performs the healing himself, and he does not use word alone for the operation, having supported all through the command for the adornment; he healed the paralytic with two words; but he also heals the blindness now with mouth and hands and much other foresight, so that he might instill firm faith through things into the unbelieving.

He stoops upon the ground and works a clot with saliva, using the earth for this purpose toward the healing, so that he might show how from that clay, whence in the beginning the living creature was formed in its entirety, a complete part is being made from the remainder. With saliva he takes this up and joins together what was scattered and unattached, so that he might show us clearly that by the power of his mouth the Word set all things in order. For by the word the heavens were established (Ps 33:5), and by the spirit of his mouth all their power (Job 33:4).

Perhaps also because of this he heals by stooping, so that those about to insult a little later with spittle might be subdued by fear; and yet the insolence of the madmen did not cease, but he was spat upon much by the...

Such things are achieved through a fall. In this first act, the creative power is shown, and by the command to wash in the pool of Siloam, the salvation through water is demonstrated to us, which the one sent (Siloam) granted to all. For then we see well when we are cleansed by the mystical water; then the light of grace surrounds us, when the power of baptism washes away the stain of sins and the spots. And all who obey the command of Siloam see the spiritual light, which enlightens every man coming into the world. Oh, the wonder and the great energy!

The man, blind a moment ago, went out from the pool with his face adorned by the addition to his eyes, seeing accurately toward the solar ray. The matter astonished the neighbors and the acquaintances. The new manner of the healing disturbed his life; the man was surrounded by the city, seeing that the work was becoming known by all, new and paradoxical, by Jesus born in Bethlehem, that little infant who was laid in the manger among the rushes. For these are the things which caused the Jews to disbelieve in the divinity.

Not then, O foolish and hard-hearted ones, apply your reasoning to the men of the age. Beginning from Adam, investigate all the following, if you find what has happened now and has been done upon others, having a life that is a model of such a healing; and again, at the dragging away of my Lord, you bring forward the child of the carpenter, whose brothers you know, whose house you know. Count all the lowly things, contend, and pour out much of our dishonor. But if neither man has done anything of this kind, nor has life had such a story, having recognized your own ignorance, look back toward the truth. Wash also yourselves in the Siloam, so that you do not perish in blindness.

But nothing was as it should be regarding them. Neither a word instructed, nor a deed taught, nor the energy of wonders nourished; but on the contrary, through innate ignorance, they attempted in myriad ways to obscure and to drag away; and malice turned back upon them to the contrary. For as much as they disbelieved, and asking...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Inheritance of Unbelief
english: They strove to overturn it, for the truth was being made more certain by so much. And he suffered the same from the beasts as those, having been wounded by something and not yet having received the whole point in the stomach, with a rush and rivalry, concentrating all the iron upon itself.

7.8.1 First, meddlingness: if this same man, and not another in his place, was shown; this being clearly testified by the man, who cried out and clearly reported the sequence of the healing, that even the mud was used as a medicine for the blindness, and that the washing of the mud in the pool provided sight. These things the neighbors investigated and learned; the Pharisees sought and did not believe.

7.8.2 Second, a technique for the invalidation of what had happened was taken up, to try to show that Christ is not the one who worked the healing. Since the man cried out to the Savior and gave back the grace by his confession and his proclamation, and made public the benefactor, they, being prevented in their mouths, reeling in their opinion, having nothing what to do, 7.8.3 run back again to the inquiry of the passion, and whether he was blind from birth; they investigate this and search the parents of the man, becoming precise examiners of each person, not in order to confirm what was done, but in order that they might receive an overturning of the wonder from somewhere and, having constructed some false pretense, might overturn the believing crowd by a rush. Oh, the excess of wickedness!

7.8.4 To fight against the truth and not to worship the one doing these things, but to drag through the dirt the benefactor; not to marvel at the power, but to disparage by trying the matters. Be persuaded even by the parents, O Pharisees, that the man was born with the blindness; and yet again you run back to the blind man, from the second and third, being informed by him of the evil attempts and the plots.

7.8.5 But whenever you fall from the first trial, you move to the second; whenever from the second, to the third; whenever from the third, to the next. As a fox is running through paths, and everywhere you are surrounded by the nets of the truth; but the exit from the wonder is without escape. However, not of all...

You are weaving a web of deceit, making it colorful indeed, but attacking weakly and without permanence. This sickness is your inheritance. You are children like unbelieving fathers. Such were they also in their manner regarding the wonders in Egypt. They were being saved from wars in a new way, yet they disbelieved the one giving salvation even though they were saved by hope. They were being fed with foods surpassing nature, and among those who were starving, they were even more ungrateful; they received manna sent from heaven, and they even craved the stench of the Egyptian leeks and onions. They were shaded during the day by a pillar of cloud so that they would not be afflicted by the heat of the solar ray, and in the night they seized a pillar of fire, having taken another new luminary distinct from the moon, and as if enjoying no divine energy, they thus sought new and celestial gods, profiting from them, so that Moses, having been detained a little on the mountain in the giving of the law, might draw them back to the return.

You truly are heirs of that ignorance, not having loved the law and hating the grace, needing not a rod of carob for supervision, but an iron one. You see a man who has passed into light, yet has remained inactive in his senses until far into his age, being led by alien eyes, sitting daily before the temple, practicing the craft of misfortune so that he might draw many into pity, the city having a witness to the suffering, seeing now and being healed quickly, not by various medicinal compositions, nor by iron cuts, but by clay alone, and this happening through saliva.

And how have you not been placed, not been struck with amazement, not casting down to the earth, worshiping the one who created the eyes from the earth, and respecting the divine energy? Instead, you are bursting with envy and you pursue God as a rival craftsman, as creators pursuing a creator, as those of the same kind pursuing the one of the same kind. And encountering old books, how many were written during the economy of the people, and how many clearly teach the reigns of kings and the history concerning them, receive the things said about each one with obedience, as some consider Moses to be a small god and exult over Elisha and his teacher...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Poverty of the Speaker vs. the Greatness of the Subject
english: Praising the Thespian and all the saints of every generation who were activated by God and performed great and unsung deeds, lifting them to the rank of angels. Do not contend regarding the ancients, nor reject the explanation of the fathers, for these things are not easily brought to the faith of hearing for natural men.

What you see now with your eyes, and what it is possible to touch with fingers and perceive accurately by sense, you simultaneously work evil against in unfaithfulness and without judgment, trampling on prophecy and reversing the outcome of foretellings. For what is seen now in the trial is what Isaiah taught of old through his words: 'Behold, our God will render judgment and will render it back; He will come and will save us. Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened and the ears of the deaf shall hear; then the lame shall leap like a deer and the tongue of the mute shall sing' (Isaiah 35:5-6).

These are not the words of Peter and John, nor are the words of any of the new and subordinate persons, so that having understood a gifted euphemism, you might reject the truth, but rather the words of your own prophecy, if you make known the Thespian, the son of Amos, a prophet, a child of a prophet, an Israelite man of the race, the head of the guidance according to the law. Glory to God, power, honor, now and always and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

All these customs, performed according to the law of the honors of the martyrs, are holy festivals and enduring monuments of those who showed courage according to God; in which the leaders of the churches, when they arrive to speak, having examined their own powers against the greatness of the matters, immediately flee in preambles toward forgiveness and entreaty and say...
Thus the majesty of the things [spoken of] is diminished by the smallness of the word.

If those who intend to praise each of the martyrs individually forbid praise, and confess their own weakness with a bright voice, what could I become today, having the teachers of the martyrs set before me for eulogy—the genuine and first disciples of Christ, the fathers of the churches, the only faithful preachers of the gospel, those who spoke with God and received the voice from God with their ears? Not so; since the word is very lofty and the undertaking difficult, let us not love the idle and inactive silence, like the cowards and the sea-fearing, who, fleeing from the mere sight of the sea, neither endure to set a ship upon the beginning nor to sail around small shores for the sake of an attempt; but let us trust in those thrice-blessed ones, and let us attempt to offer the things according to power to the joy of the others, regarding the undertaking as that for which we have been liberated today.

For I know that this will be sought not so much as it is owed to those great and wondrous ones, but as much as can be found by us, the poor. Therefore, I desired that a small part of that grace might be granted to me today, of which each of these saints, having taken hold, either in Jerusalem taught those who were disobedient, or in Athens, having grasped the Arian error, turned back those who were superstitious by showing them Christ and announcing the mystery of true piety. For thus we have demonstrated something of what is set to be accomplished, and have not left behind much of the greatness.

Since the great gifts of the Spirit are great things, and I am unworthy to be enriched by such a grace, I will add poverty to my willingness toward you, just as Elisha [added] vegetables to the lentils...

title: The Foundation of the Church
english: Goodness will certainly not be deprived of honor. No one should think that I, following the praise of brave men heard from you, will follow the laws of the wisdom of the outside. For we do not practice flattery through a composed art, but we strive to present to you, souls desiring virtue, the truth. Therefore, the silence of lineage and the pride of fathers will not obstruct the word. Flesh and blood shall not inherit the kingdom of God (Romans 8:3). Nor shall we honor the sky-dwellers from the worldly and earth-bound, but rather the opposite: the obscure lives of fathers, the crude arts, and the shadow called poverty shall be remembered in praises.

For the glory of Christians, according to the gospel, is our humility. I am also terribly reproached by the praises of those from without, because they, wishing to ennoble those they win over, say nothing exceptional, but they sit by the graves and disturb those lying there, making the dead into a decoration for the living; through which they call upon the departed, while confessing they have nothing good to say to those being praised by them.

And besides this, if it were true that those descending from illustrious fathers are themselves good and inherit virtue as if by some nature, it would perhaps have been timely to make some mention of the parents; but since the successions of lineage are lied about, there is even more difference in outward affectations; for the philosopher is unrefined and the lover of pleasure is a philosopher, and it is useless to remember the toil of the forefathers; it is necessary to demonstrate, if anyone has achievements of virtue. And to learn that this has such a way, one cannot learn it from meddling elsewhere, but from our own Holy Scripture, having manifold and varied usefulness.

Know certainly the priest, that elder, the nourisher and teacher of the great Samuel; but he himself, being excellent, did not benefit the sons; and having been nourished by him who begot [him] and learning the laws of the priesthood every day. And from ungodly fathers again, I speak of Timothy, the brave dog of Paul the apostle, and he certainly did not follow as if by some nature of the parents.
Having judged by reason, he hated their impiety toward the holy law of piety, and a sweet fruit appeared from a bitter root. Half-men in communion and sheep in offspring.

Thus Absalom, having been a youth toward a lenient father and so well known for audacity, as much as the father was in kindness; or rather, if it is necessary to speak the truer thing, he exceeded by a great measure in wickedness the virtue of the one who begat him. And entirely, if anyone wishes to understand with the mind this opposition of children toward fathers, he will find myriads of the diligent from the evil and the wicked from the best. And very appropriately. For if nature and not manner were performing virtue or wickedness, the two would not be, but one side would have prevailed alone.

Let Peter be called the son of Jonah; as for whose [son] this is, it makes no difference to me. For I honor the one who begat through the actions of the son; and starting from below, I send the glory to the things above, just as the lamps of the night light the ceilings from the ground. He says, prophesying Isaiah, that the Father placed the Son as a cornerstone, indicating that the whole composition of the world has its seat and its foundation in Him.

And the Only-begotten again, as he says in the gospels, names Peter the foundation of the church: 'You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church.' For truly this one is first like a great and enduring stone cast into the hollow of this world or the pit of lamentation, as David says, so that having supported all Christians remaining in building, he might lift them up to the height, which is the dwelling-place of our hope. Paul also calls Christ the foundation, saying: 'No one can lay a foundation other than the one laid, which is Jesus Christ.'

Our Savior, by the same designation, adorned even his first disciple, naming him a rock of faith. Therefore, through Peter, the foundation of the churches is saved, being unshakeable and unswerving, having become a true and faithful initiate of piety. Through the building of the righteous we have stood rooted, Christians from the setting sun until the rising. And having been moved by many trials since it was reported that the...

title: Theologian vs. Human Wisdom
english: The Gospel, wanting to cast down myriads of tyrants and even the devil before them and to bring us down to the ground with their foundations. Indeed the 36 rivers flowed, as the saving word says, like torrents, and fierce winds of devilish spirits struck, and the rains of those persecuting Christians burst through, and nothing stronger was seen of the fortification according to God, because the building of faith was constructed with the holy stones of the first of the apostles.

These things happened because of one word of blessing, naming the evangelist Peter. Let us see, if it seems good, how Peter builds: not with stones and bricks, nor with other earthly materials, but with words and actions made effective by the Spirit.

Therefore, when our God and Savior ascended into the heavens, while the cloud was a vehicle for the apostles to see, this man took up the teaching of the Gospel; and before all those sharing in the episcopate, opening the mouth of those raging against piety, he purified a people, and a wise orator appeared among the nations and Israel; people whose teeth were sharpened and whose minds were filled, if anyone should name Jesus.

So that what was said concerning the Lord by prophecy fits perfectly also with Peter: 'Many dogs have surrounded me, fattened bulls have enclosed me' (Psalm 71:9). But nevertheless, living by the Spirit and not grasping the command but saving what was said to him: 'Feed my lambs' (John 21:15), he cried out to a mixed people from myriads of nations; Jewish men and all those dwelling in Jerusalem.

And so that we may not speak at length, joining all the discourse together, he remembers the sayings of Joel prophesying the outpouring of the Spirit (Joel 2:28); from there he moves to David, setting forth the fifteenth psalm to confirm the resurrection (Psalm 16:10); and concluding the whole word in wisdom of words and witness of the law, he immediately led the listeners on, not ten, nor a hundred, nor three or five times so many, but three thousand men, a fullness of the church, a whole people sufficient to strike the enemies, of whom they burst through in a crowd.
Oh, how persuasive a warm and fiery medicine, having cleansed the souls so sharply! Oh, wisdom!

Theologian, having covered all human wisdom! What do you say, you who crown Demosthenes according to rhetoricians and praise Socrates among philosophers? For Demosthenes, indeed, the great and much-talkative one regarding rhetoric, held himself back so much from those things he intended to persuade by, that he was even exiled from the city by the listeners; but Socrates, for the many discourses toward the Athenians and the wise discussions, found the end in the hemlock, being killed by the chorus of disciples; such was his extent in the power of persuading.

But Peter the fisherman, the craftsman, the unlearned, whom anyone would call whatever they might wish to belittle, having hunted three thousand men with a single thrust of a word, firmly established [the church]; and these, being discontented and rioting and not forgiving him the dividing of the beginning, split the mouth.

But having come to a sufficient increase and progress of the Christian rank, since he provided a wonderful experience toward logical teachings and exhortations and practical power, having just set the lame man upright from the temple porches, that lame man who had suffered the disease from the stroke of nature in the womb of a mother, all the people rushed to the temple, being led by the fame of the great work toward the sight, and all were looking intently at the man, being struck with amazement at the wonder; the mouths of the enemies of Christ were stopped, and the cross remained a trophy of victory, not a dream.

Again the uneducated one, the worker of the prostitute's craft, begins to speak words a second time toward them, saying: 'O men, if what has happened appears to you worthy of a wonder and of divine energy, worship the healer of the lame, Jesus, whom you despised and lastly, having surpassed [him] with anger, raised up on the wood. This one is and lives; and just as it was said to you many times, having risen from the dead, he reigns over all things.'

So now, therefore, having taken up the care of those among you who have sinned, come to him and be enlightened, just as your father David says (Psalm 110:4). For if you are sons of the prophets and disciples of Moses, do not dishonor the grace of your ancestors by paying attention to lying words, but having wisely observed those things proclaimed by them, receive with your souls the Savior of your race. For this is he whom...

title: The greatness of Peter's miracles
english: And Moses promised that a prophet would rise up for you (Deut 18:15). Having passed through these and such things to the people, he went away, adding others as many as the three thousands.
Such a man was indeed bold in speaking publicly, eager, undaunted, and wise for the guidance into the mysteries of the gospel, making the cowardice of his own and of his opponents a terror.

Because it was not only most diligent for the most excellent teacher of piety to labor for the great number of God's people, but much more to have the disciples live strictly according to the laws given, he saw that Ananias—that one who was a thief of his own fruits and intended to introduce a strange sacrilege and a bad habit of sin to the Christians—and he decisively cut him off from the church; he was not being crude or murderous in his intention, but in view of the purpose of benefit, he thus treated the sin as a physician.

For since the people were new converts and newly pure, having received the evangelical laws from the mixture of Greek and Jewish ways, it is expected that the disciples need not only verbal admonition, but also some practical fear; for men have somewhat habituated themselves so that, in order that they might be regulated in the beginnings of their customs, they might keep the habit until their end.

And because of this, having exposed the sin, he immediately brought death as the punishment, not using a sword, nor handing him over to executioners, but then showing the power of Christ differently in the manner of the removal. For he summoned, and the one summoned, having fallen, expired. How great this is, and how much reverence he worked in the church, we do not need to learn.

For two things were achieved in one: that our Savior be believed to be God, and that the teacher of his laws has angels accompanying him, ready, working according to the will of the apostle. He wished to benefit the lame, and the grace was not slow; he willed to punish the sacrilege, and the punishment occurred.

These things are sufficient to strike even stony souls and to persuade them firmly, that the words spoken by Peter (Acts 5:3-4) were not a deception; but God was with him and the mystery which he announced was holy and true. And it is necessary to attend to this, that the [thing] on the [other hand]...

A sign was once provided by the apostle through necessity, in folly and murder, so that those with evil intentions might be shown the power of punishment. However, the performance of benefits and healings occurred daily and continuously, and such ease and grace surrounded him in healing, so that no sick person who approached left deceived of hope, but went home whole and healthy. And every place in Jerusalem where Peter appeared to speak Christ was a place, and the crowd of following sick people had a daily wondrous spectacle from a mixed multitude, some gathered to be freed from the evils of the crowd, others to behold those being healed.

Thus also that wonderful thing concerning the apostle is written, which was not said of any of the others, that the relatives and the households of the sick brought them upon beds publicly, so that even the shadow of Peter, when he came, might overshadow some of them. This indeed is already greater than the Lord's own wonders, and the servant is praised above the Lord. And perhaps in this sign the prophecy is fulfilled, which the Savior made to the disciples: 'Amen, amen I say to you: the one believing in me the works which I do, he will do also, and he will do greater things than these' (John 14:12).

When I say this, I do not compare the servant to the Master. Away! The thought is going mad; but that God, by showing His own power through those healing by His own [power], enriched none of the disciples like Peter with his own gifts, but rather set him above all by gifts from above; and just as he became the first disciple according to the order of time, so he was shown greater than the brothers in the experience of things by the power of the Spirit.

He was called first and quickly obeyed; found by the seashores in the turbulent region of the world, always surrounded by waves and the ceaseless sound crying around the winds. He was the first among Christians to think of cosmic things, transcending all those in all things, and he was transferred toward the intelligible and the super-cosmic. And perhaps someone of the poor and obscure says, calling that thrice-blessed one: 'What...'
