title: The Wealth of Faith and the Crossing of the Seas
english: For what did he set aside? And what did he acquire? Everything that he had, O man; and to each person, what he possesses is great; and that also is wealth, which he holds as a steward. He appears similar before God, both he who laid aside the chariot and he who despised the donkey. For just as a chariot is to the rich man, so a humble basket is to the poor man.

8.9.2 Likewise, a philosopher is he who left behind the silver table adorned with histories, and he who left the wooden one; likewise, he who left the populous village and he who left the small garden; he who left the gold-embroidered garment and he who left the worn-out tunic. For God does not judge the giver by the abundance or the quality of the things given, but He accepts the choice of the one giving.

8.9.3 Therefore, even that widow, the Gospel proclaims her as praiseworthy (Luke 21:2), she who gave the mite, because she did not set aside anything from what she had. And he who, reaching for the cup, took the cold water, receives as a reward for such easy generosity the kingdom; for he served the need of the thirsty with what he had, even if wine of spring-bloom was not present to him because of poverty.

8.9.4 Now I say these things by way of concession, since not always is a fisherman also a poor man. Do you not know that a fisherman is a hunter of pearls? But pearls are the bloom of the sardine and of exalted wealth, with which kings are adorned, and in which women are praised as lovers of wealth and lovers of beauty. A fisherman dyes the many-threaded and consecrated purple; fishermen dye the yellow pigment of the fields by hunting the sub-golden ones.

8.9.5 Therefore, it is not necessary to pay attention to the tools of their craft as if they were luxurious and highly esteemed—the net, I say, and the hooks; for it is not from the cheapness of the tools in each case, but from the completed work that prosperity is perceived; since, according to that same logic, you would find nothing poorer than agriculture, if [judging] from the hoe and the spade.

That its wealth might be tested. And those mining gold are utterly without resources, lacking the King of wealth. For a single value works for them: a wooden table, which separates the gold of the earth.

Be silent, then, both Gentiles and Hebrews, those insulting Peter for his poverty and attempting to belittle the fisherman by his former state; and having left such things, let them tell me, as I inquire: Which fisherman or which of all men has crossed the sea? Who set foot by a standing lake, as he did by the waves tossing in the winds? For our good God has performed many wonders through His own servants, even regarding the ancient polity of Israel, and even in later times, in which the Philanthropic Economy of our Savior has appeared to the world, no one from the beginning to the end of the saints seems to have accomplished such a deed through his own faith and the grace from above.

Moses was wonderful, having crossed the sea without ships; but he reached a land which was a law to men, from where the water was drawn back to itself. Great also is Jesus, the successor of this, because He crossed the Jordan while the banks were overflowing; but likewise, crossing the Red Sea, He cut the stream and gave the crossing people a dry path for their advance.

But no man ever raised his foot upon the water. For even the law of nature does not allow a liquid substance, flowing and changing, to withstand the solid and pressing. It seems to me that the Lord and Master of all, having been greatly amazed at such a ready willingness of the man, cried out saying: 'Command me to come to you upon the waters,' as a reward for that much love and faith, to give him that new and paradoxical grace, of which Peter alone appeared receptive from those of Adam until the end of men. For truly and exceptionally from God is the...

title: The Economy of Christ and the Seed of Truth
english: Such a display of a great work surpasses the lowly nature of creation, just as it seems to David, the best of the prophets. For he also, in one of the psalms, while hymnologizing God and explaining His unsearchable and incomprehensible nature, said with power those things which you know from the usual chanting: 'Your way is in the sea, and your paths are in many waters, and your tracks will not be known' (Ps 77:19).

Therefore, what the Master had for His own in the exceptional knowledge of divinity, He made common to the servant, judging him worthy of such honor. Indeed, the zealous and great John was resting on the Lord's bosom; great was also James, being called the son of thunder; and glorious in honors was Philip, who, having been snatched away by the Spirit, initiated the Ethiopian to the knowledge of the Savior. Nevertheless, let all yield to Peter and confess him to be second, when the comparison of gifts tests who is preferred.

But reviewing all things individually and examining, I find this man leaping ahead of all the other disciples everywhere, both in logical discourses and in practical activities, and standing out, and afterwards leaving behind those running the same stage of life. For the Lord once asked the Twelve, testing how they might have certainty and opinion regarding their assumption of Him, and commanding them to speak clearly what they say He is, while all the others were deliberating in silence, being slow and showing that they were agonizing over the response due to some hesitation; he, opening his mouth quickly, bearing the coal of faith upon his soul which previously purified Isaiah's lips, truly confessed that blessed and wise utterance: 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God' (Mt 16:16).

Who then would marvel at anyone worthy of these words, having become a reliable interpreter of the greatest of the apostles? For see first how the word is concise and brief, expressing the power of myriads of things in a short exclamation. For every such word is excellent, which is appropriate and whose phrasing does not overflow, being concise in its meaning. On the contrary, a multitude of things...

In brief, it signifies according to the likeness of a mustard seed, which is very small when being held and looked at, but if you bring it to the sense of the mouth, the whole animal is drawn from feet to head toward its home by heat.

You are the Christ, the Son of the living God (1 John 5:20). Every word contributing to the knowledge of God and our Savior is viewed and directed toward these two things: one is that of the primordial deity, which is the Word in the beginning, who is always and being with the Father and being God (John 1:1), just as the great John the Theologian initiated us, like a sponge lying against the breast of the Only-begotten and from there drawing out the knowledge of the hidden truth; the other is that of the economy, which the good God accepted for the condescension of our weakness.

It is therefore worthy to observe the response, how in brevity and conciseness he most accurately revealed the mind in a few words, beginning from the lower things and leading the mind upward toward the high things step by step.

You are the Christ. This is a declaration of the economy and an explanation of the incarnate theophany. For this is not the name of the pre-eternal Word, but the message of the graces being used. Therefore also our Lord, having accepted entirely to become man and all the other things that turn toward the flesh, condescends and is called Christ as one anointed for king, not with the oil of the horn like Samuel and David and the men following them (1 Sam 16:13), but by the energy of the Spirit, by which also the Lord is anointed. For thus Jesus was marvelously made known and paradoxically presented to many to commune with, in the womb of the Virgin.

Having confessed Jesus, the man who became for our sake, he did not set this word until this point, but having ascended toward heaven by the intellectual Jacob's ladder (Gen 28:12) and having become in the vision of the God-Word in the beginning, he added to him the exceptional and true dignity, addressing him as Son of the living God. And precisely thus and not otherwise: he himself, having confessed the straight and incorruptible rule of faith and having handed to us all an unshakeable law of piety, did not depart unrewarded or unhonored; but blessed [is the name]...

title: The Shepherd's Commission and the Martyrdom of Polycarp
english: Having been received from the truly blessed one, he is called the rock of faith and the foundation and the substructure of the church according to Christ. He receives the keys through the promise of the kingdom and becomes lord of those gates, so as to open them to whomever he wishes and to close them to whomever is just, but certainly to the unfaithful and the impious and those denying that same confession, through which he was appointed to stand as an exact guardian of the entrances of the kingdom, as a faithful one of the good things.

Oh, the darkness and the cloudiness which has poured out much before the eyes of men, through which the heretics do not see the traces of the fathers, nor are they able even to walk in them, which the feet of the apostles have worn down. For behold, Peter, the genuine disciple of Christ by election, having received everywhere the first vote and the honors and the achievements, that great one who was all, whose fame filled the whole inhabited world, having been commanded to speak so as to glorify our God and Savior, did not begin a wandering from some distance away, nor, surrounding himself with a circle of syllogisms and matters, he answered toward the question as if now the terrible sophists and technicians of faith are accustomed to do, but in simplicity of heart he set forth the truth briefly, not sending the unbegotten to the begotten, nor having reasoned excessively about the similar and the dissimilar, nor having busied himself with differences concerning all substance, nor having measured the immeasurable divinity with syllogisms, like the plays of Arius and the maneuvers of Eunomius.

Let us therefore, O Christians, zealously imitate the knowledge of the fisherman, the unsearching one, the elder from Bethsaida, the first catch of Christ, whose knowledge is not much talk. Let us meditate on saying: 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God' (Matt 16:16), and to leave the more [complex things] to the word-fighters, whose strife is their work and whose end is destruction. Does the apostle's miracles stand until what has been said? Or do we think that quite the opposite would not even come to pass, if someone were to deviate from the things spoken, remaining beside them? But I, leaving the many things to your own knowledge, for you know Peter and his [deeds], even if no one should precede me in praising the man, I wish to speak small things concerning his rest and how...
He escaped from the earth to heaven, so that there he might cease to say 'wherever that life is'.

Our Savior, as He was about to approach the arbitrary death, like an exceptional deposit, entrusts the general and ecumenical church to this man, asking him for the third time, 'Do you love me?' (John 21:15). Since he eagerly set forth the confessions in equal number to the questions, he took the world into his care as one shepherd, having heard, 'Feed my lambs' (John 21:15); and almost instead of himself, the Lord gave to the converts a father, a shepherd, and a teacher.

Having heard this voice, therefore, he did not live his life in idleness, nor did he love the life of danger outside, but he was encircling the whole inhabited world, revealing Christ to those becoming blind, guiding those wandering, strengthening those having tasted salvation, fighting against enemies, exhorting those at home, enduring persecutions, bearing the burden of prisons, and risking the gospel in many ways.

As time passed, having seized the ruling city of men, he ascended from there to the kingdom. For Nero, being thrown into anger, surpassed all other modes of torture, just as once in Palestine when Herod was king and the Magi were announcing Christ, exceeding the others in his ways of punishment, it was decreed that the thrice-blessed one should be crucified on the wood of a cross, so that Peter the Lord's disciple might not only imitate him in walking the sea (Matt 14:29), but also in hanging upon the wood.

However, as a pious and wise man, even knowing the time of struggle, he asked of the enemies just one difference: that they might not bring him in a similar form to the wood, but rather having crucified the head to the lower part of the cross. For it is not worthy, even in equal suffering, for the slave to encounter the same as the Master. He said, and it happened as he willed, and through the cross he departed to the one crucified and risen, himself having put on the crown of martyrdom, leaving to us the causes of these feasts.

title: The Transformation of Paul
english: A participant in your virtue, Tarso, who through a different mode of punishment, but with a single purpose of piety, analyzed himself with you toward Christ. Paul the lawgiver, the loud-voiced trumpet of the gospel, who formerly was a bitter enemy of Christians, but finally a strong advocate for the church, was more recently reached by the apostles through grace; and in time he was second among the disciples of Christ, but equal according to the proven virtue, so that I may say nothing more than to exceed the twelve in redness. He was a zealous follower of Moses, if anyone else was, a wall of the law, a tower of the Old Testament, enduring and unshakeable; and until he held his purpose unchangeable, there was a great danger to those speaking of Christ, and he fled everywhere from our [people]. Truly, according to the prophecy of Jacob (Gen 49:10), a wolf snatched the Benjamin, tearing the lambs of the New Testament and scattering the flocks.

Because he also performed the drama according to Saint Stephen, and having his hands still stained with blood, he ran toward Damascus, seeking to join persecution to persecution and murder to murder, and to uproot Christianity, the first blooming nature. Our God saw well what he had done, that the strong enemy might become a noble friend; and having suddenly surrounded him with light, He strikes him with astonishment and changes him toward humility, making him stand in the road through fear, and having brought to sobriety the eyes that were looking with fiery and angry temper through the darkness. And He punishes him not in silence, but also added a word to the deed, saying that written thing: 'Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? It is hard for you to kick against the pricks' (Acts 26:14). For it was not as if he himself needed a discussion, since the words of the facts were sufficient, but so that he might have an occasion within to ask and to learn that he who was thought to be dead and to be Christ lives, and appears from the heavens, and thus defends those who are grieving from authority. Nothing is more like the words themselves to explain to us the hunt of the Hebrew wolf.
And Saul, still breathing threats and murder, the word describes to me a man whose mind is being shattered by the [pressure]...

While the mixed nature of the event was still being perceived through the whistling of the stones, seeing a wind and a wild thing as if it were the murderer, the symbols were being saved in the beginning of the patriarch's prophecy. For he, since he was about to die, having surrounded his children from every side, foretold by the Spirit at the bedside.

Thus, while blessing Judah, he was speaking in one way, but allegorically he praised the Christ coming from him. Furthermore, having prophesied to all the things to come, he came last upon Benjamin, who was also more recent in time; and at times he spoke toward the son, but in reality he signified Paul, as we know, descending from that tribe. 'Benjamin is a wolf; in the morning he shall snatch, and in the evening he shall deliver prey' (Gen 49:27).

Let us investigate what is said. Is it certainly this: that after having eaten the first things—that is, having pursued, having murdered, having shed blood, having scattered the church like a flock—he became last a shepherd and a good pastor, having laid aside the persecutor and having put on the apostle, distributing to all as food the Word and having established this holy table for us?

For the power of the Lord is such, disarming the fury and the impious thoughts of those standing in opposition, and approaching gracefully and subduing, working to make sheep by day instead of beasts that tear. Upon this, what does the Scripture say? That having approached the high priest, he requested from him letters to the synagogues in Damascus, so that he might bring the Christians to Jerusalem (Acts 9:2).

O what a fight and a difference of letters, those then being sought from Paul and those which he later wrote announcing Christ! Some were binding Christians, while others put on the chains for Christ, causing the persecutor to endure many heavy and difficult things; and there it was written: 'Saul, a Hebrew, a defender of the law, an enemy of the cross, an opponent of the gospel'; but in the later and more temperate letters: 'Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ.' Of whom? Add this: of him who was crucified.

O what a wonder! What a moment ago was a dream, now has become a boast, and what was being reviled is remembered today as glory. For no glory-seeker and boastful king has thus sent forth the splendor of the beginning.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Conversion of Paul
english: Just as Paul writes himself to be all a prisoner and more polished by iron than women are by the gold used for adornment, suddenly a light from heaven surrounded him. Why does he not appear to him in the form of a man, just as [it was for] Stephen from heaven, but rather in the appearance of fire or light?

Because Stephen, being perfect and knowing the mystery of the incarnation, and being harmed nothing by our poverty, thus beautifully showed himself and so ascended into heaven; but for Paul, so that he might not be restrained from calling Jesus God, since he had come to us in a body, he does not appear as a man, lest he might confirm the unbelieving opposition, but rather in the idea of a flash and light, so that he might draw him from the law and Moses. For there also the same God, manifesting himself to Moses, burned in fire; and giving the law on Sinai, he was handing the tablets to the Hebrew, shining with fire. Therefore, it surrounds him so that, having cast his mind upon the likeness of those things occurring then and now, and as if having awakened himself from a certain forgetfulness, he might know the theophanies to be one power; and he sends the radiance from heaven, so that Paul, no longer turning his mind around Bethlehem and Galilee, calling Christ the son of David and man and all the other names of the economy, might be clearly taught that being God, he came down from above, which is why he now appears.

Then he adds wisely: 'I am Jesus'; he did not say 'I am God' or 'the Son of God', but 'Jesus'; the name of the condescension, so that he might confirm the faith of the incarnation, at which the Jews were stumbling. 'I am he whom you crucify, whom you imprison, whom you drag and lead now to Caiaphas, and later to Pilate, whom you constantly call the son of the carpenter, whom you count among the dead, laughing greatly...'

To those proclaiming the resurrection. I do not seem to be speaking to them now; being present, I do not see; lighting the soul, I have brought blindness to the eyes. Believe, therefore, that I also appeared to Stephen while saying this to you and he believed. It is, therefore, harsh for you to strike against spikes. 'Spikes' means the nails of the cross. For just as one, being struck by iron, is being split open, does he not destroy that? For how does one destroy the hard? But he wounds himself; even so, the one contending against God seizes destruction upon himself headlong.

Be prudent, therefore, and having lost your sight, now especially through the wonderful flash of light, consider that for this reason I clothed myself with a body and became a man, so that not all the naked ones, approaching the veil of divinity, might be blinded.

These things: and Paul, being led by the hand, was being led as a pitiable sight, but rather as something graceful and worthy of indignation. The wolf was bound, the rapacious man became prudent, the wild man was gentled, the runner walked meekly, the tyrant among the disciples was being led, he whose hands were stained with the blood of Stephen, seeking to drink the blood of the other. And for three days he continued living in blindness. And most appropriately. For he, having justly protested against the Trinity, was condemned to an equal measure of punishment to sin. Thus, indeed, the law-giver was initiated into piety. And since he had tasted the truth and through experience learned that Christ lives and is and reigns over all things, neither was he destroyed by death nor was he stolen away by the disciples, having quickly been transferred from the law to the gospel, he announced God, the Christ, to all, whom yesterday and formerly he mocked with blasphemies, and such a man was an ally just as he was an enemy; for he was strong in both. And entering unannounced and unexpectedly into the synagogues of Damascus, he was expounding the words of the law and the prophets, not holding to the law, but constructing and comparing from it the Christ to those things coming to pass.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Paul's Unwavering Ministry
english: By these things, casting out law by law through the law. Just as he says about himself in writing to the Romans: 'For I died by law through law'; that is, having been led by the Mosaic writings, he came to know the piety of the gospel. 8.25.3 Therefore he caused a marvel in Damascus, and all were exclaiming to themselves: 'Come, behold the Tarsian Jew, a zealous student of the ancestral law, a fierce advocate for Jesus, calling Him up and proving from our writings that this is the Savior according to the promise.' Lest the fear not persuade the whole city, might not the whole people be led and turn away from the law? 8.25.4 For he is a practitioner of the Scripture, and sharp of mind, and the word is rapid, and the method resourceful, and he has possessed much reliability; from which, knowing our writings accurately, he does not seem to wander in ignorance, but has found the truth through testing and judgment. Into this perplexity he cast a great city, a populous people, the first preaching of the brave convert; and then Damascus was more troubled than Jerusalem previously was when Christians were being stoned, when Stephen Paul was stoning. 8.25.5 Just as the wonderful ones of the best men, wherever they are transferred, carry the victory there, so that lawgiver man always made those people great by the momentum he provided.

8.26.1 Thus then, having proclaimed the gospel in Phoenicia and having cast the first seeds of the apostolate there, where he himself was also enlightened by knowledge, he came to Jerusalem, a stranger to those there and a fine spectacle. For those who had sent him forward and given the bonds to carry against Christians, not knowing what was happening in the midst, first saw him pleasantly and were eager for the hunt, a multitude of Christian prisoners, hoping to see and seeking the work of the many promises. 8.26.2 But when the word was going forth, I found Paul joining Saul, agreeing in his conviction and being a more fervent disciple of Christ and of the other apostles; at first they considered the things said to be childishness and mockery, but having tested him, they found him confessing the conviction with his voice, and they deliberated only on one thing: that the young man should be released, as it was not fitting for the Hebrew religion.
And to serve the living Paul and his speaking. And later time clearly showed this.

For even among the many, although they were already Christians, they were not sufficient to live purely according to the gospel, but were wavering and sometimes even coloring [their faith] with circumcision, in order that they might appease the wrath of the Hebrews by partially performing what was granted to them; but this man alone, without yielding anything by an unshakeable mindset, taught, but with a pure voice he proclaimed the word without derivation and progressed so far into the freedom of mindset, that once, regarding the Galatians' domestic dullness and the scarcity of those teaching, he wrote a letter to them against the wonderful life of retreating into the law (cf. Galatians 6:12), by which he taught them to worship and practice religion in the novelty of the citizenship according to Christ, no longer paying attention to the writings from the stone tablets.

He remained bound to what was said of him as the foremost of the apostles and was being purified everywhere, and he fought against Peter, as if Peter were attacking the new citizenship by the use of the old and ceased dogmas; and he neither loved the proximity of the elder nor the prestige of the apostleship when he saw the truth in danger. But he stood up fiercely for the Galatians, and he struck the other many times, as he was, having won the opportunity through boldness.

And everywhere he continued speaking and persuading; and if perhaps he encountered evil men and suffered something terrible, or lived in prison, or received lashes, or was thrown with stones, he did not abandon his readiness because of the occurring failure; but after a short interval, he approached the enemies again, and conversing with the same people, and discovering many ways of undertaking, and being very well-adapted to the falling needs, he went on persuading either all or the many.

And often, indeed, having been found after incurable wounds and having been cast out in the outskirts of that city which he was initiating into piety, and being thought dead because of the greatness of the terrors, having seized the next day's market and having stretched out his right hand, he again taught those who were approaching death; thus, nothing cared for his body, but looking toward the goal of the higher calling (cf. Philippians 3:14), he was patient.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Apostle's Peripatetic Ministry and the Corruption of Priests
english: He was contending from place to place, city from city, enduring earthly labors, facing the dangers from the sea, speaking wisely to inflammatory crowds, and defending himself before angry judges. He was leading the Hebrews into the knowledge of Christ through the Scriptures honored among them, and shaming the Greeks with external words and the unwritten laws of nature; he was confirming Christians, building up converts, and nourishing them with appropriate instruction, just as gardeners tend the young plants with the measured and accustomed flow of waters. Let us learn what most clearly demonstrates his strength in words.

Athens is a city presiding over Achaia, a hearth of words, as those who speak well of it have said, and an ancient workshop of wise men and of those living in words. Since therefore Paul, having run through Illyricum and scattered the sparks of faith everywhere—which, having received from the Spirit, he kept unquenchable—he came according to the necessity of the period to the wise Athenians. And it was a matter worthy of much concern, how the tentmaker might discourse the words concerning God to those who are worthy of ruling all men together according to education.

But, being uplifted by greatness of nature and the wealth of the heavenly gift, he did not take hold of one of the sheltered buildings, nor, sitting at one workshop, did he perform a dialogue, as the first of the philosophers among them were accustomed to do with those approaching; rather, running up to the Areopagus, where there was a harsh and fearful council judging with deadly trials, he found a great multitude gathered there, and stood there lecturing against the rhetoricians according to their customs, those who contended with them daily.

Taking the beginning from an inscription which was attached to an altar, and from there effectively announcing the unknown God to them and concluding with the whole Word, he abstained so much from arguing like a layman about external wisdom, that he converted Dionysius, the most prominent of the Areopagites, along with his wife, and made slaves for Christ, turning many from one altar and one small inscription into many altars.
Descending...

From there, where the warring demon of the Greeks had most power, he moved to the neighboring city, Corinth, the metropolis of Achaia. Speaking in the synagogues, he drove away the salvation-teaching, not just one of the many or those succeeding, but the chief synagogue leader along with his whole household. Having conquered the law from its peak and exalted the cross as a high trophy, he left that city having bowed to Christ.

As time passed and the word of piety was obstructed, he acted like a general, daily seizing cities, villages, and fields, cutting the sinews of the former tyrant. He moved from Corinth to the land of the Pisidians, then seized Lycaonia and the cities of Phrygia, and having visited Asia from there, then Macedonia. He was a common teacher of the inhabited world, benefiting those seeing him by his tongue, and those far away by letters. Only his knee did not tire from traveling, nor his tongue failing, as he unceasingly explained the mysteries of the gospel to enemies and friends.

But such was his teaching; what of the other philosophy of life? He who always persevered in the word and served the gospel, not even taking bread he consumed for free from anyone, but having the struggle against myriads of enemies by day, and by night the toil and the labor of his craft, so that he might have sustenance there, yet appears to all as an apostle driven forth, an unwearied herald, even sparing the bread of those he was hosting.

Let us hear these words, priests, you who do not merely share in the altars, but enrich yourselves from them and feast, making the sacred property your own private possession, and commanding the subordinates like slaves for the sake of Christ. Priesthood is not lordship, but rather for the one who understands, a service; it is not a claim of princely insolence, but an economy of pious ministry. Did not the law-giving Paul not have the authority to eat and drink from the sacred things, and even a little so...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Ministry of John and the Impact of the Word
english: Should he receive the reward of countless labors for the healing of a body being struck daily? But he did not use the authority so that, having taken nothing upon the earth, he might demand all things in the heavens. Therefore, he was even permitted to be superior to man, yet remaining bound to corruptible flesh.

8.31.3 And so that he might also see the earnest of the coming good things and the honors there, he is carried up even unto the third heaven; he sees visions surpassing the lot of those here, and hears unspeakable words, as he himself says (2 Cor 12:2), and while measuring these, he distributes everywhere the greatness and the boasting of one's own advantages. But so that he might only send down the understandings of those growing by small gifts, by necessity a few of his own are stripped bare, and these, having been placed upon another person, he leads far away from the suspicion concerning him.

8.31.4 Elijah the Thespian, indeed, since in an idea he was carried up to the height by a chariot of fire (1 Kings 18:12), is sung of everywhere and left much wonder by his life; but as far as he reached, no word has interpreted. For, by chance and being raised only a little from the earth by the driving power, he was given to the place where he had the lot to dwell. But the translation of Paul was found more brilliant and glorious, fitting the measure to which he was carried. For he reached as far as the singing of the seven heavens, though a little was lacking for the half-way point.

8.31.5 Moreover, the Hebrews cast down the understanding against Moses (Exod 19:20), thinking greatly that he alone reached to the summit of Sinai and entered within the ridge and the clouds. For my Paul, instead of a mountain, ascended toward the heavens, and instead of a cloud, wandered beyond the air which is above the cloud. And most fittingly. For it was necessary for the man according to Christ to conquer Moses so much that the Gospel surpasses the Law.

8.32.1 And in the theophanies and the things spoken by God, and how, being bound, he was loosed and, being dejected, was strengthened, and even a dream was his, God making use of him—what is there to say, when he himself did not hide his own grace, but clearly revealed it to all together, saying: 'Do you indeed seek the Christ speaking in me?' For the others, whether prophets or apostles, had timely and chronological activities from above, and at times with them...
It was the divine, and at times it was not present.

This lawgiver was, just as a special temple of God having been completed for Him for habitation, always possessed Christ as a finder of counsel, a teacher of the word, and a partner in all things. And John, the son of Zebedee, seemed great, because among the other disciples he rested boldly upon the Lord's breast (John 13:23); and because of this, he is especially unsung among all.

But this one—how could he not be justly thought to be even above men, he who daily rested not the Jesus in the body, but the Word naked of flesh (John 1:14), having established himself as a very useful and pure vessel for the Creator? And having many and various things to say, as this lawgiver said and did all things, educating the whole world upon earth and sea, in courts, in marketplaces, among the people, and in the courts of kings, intentionally surpassing the multitude.

For I did not set before myself to write a biography of what he achieved, so that nothing might be lacking, but to work a reputation, and this as far as my power reaches. But mentioning only one of the last, I will rest the word.

For since, having circled the whole inhabited world and having placed the great word upon the lamp, he lit the fire of evangelical knowledge, he arrived also at the Romans, as a ruling city, in order to, having initiated and persuaded those holding sway over all men, and having acquired disciples from the surrounding area, speak to the other men. And finding Peter there also, a fellow worker of the same zeal, and having joined a certain holy and inspired company, he educated those under the law in synagogues, and attended to the Gentiles in marketplaces; and he was a diverse teacher of good things, manifesting the pure and unblemished knowledge of God, establishing precise canons of moral virtue, driving away from men debauchery and drunkenness and all unrestrained sensuality, by which especially both the multitude and the one reigning then were held.

Thus, the introduction of the best and most temperate way gripped Nero severely; and he suffered more pain from the destruction of pleasure than if he were being cast out from his own kingship. For he was, if anyone else, a sophist of pleasures.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Learning through Practice and Example
english: Living in luxury and wasting away, a weakling and a woman's slave, a profligate of lust, [he is] not a king of men. For how could he have ruled others without first learning to rule himself? He set one care, so that he might cut off from the city the teacher of piety and self-control.

And, jealous of Herod's mindset, he led the apostles into prison, just as that [Herod] did to John; but having, in similarity, another Herodias, the unrestrained and lustful-minded one, seeking the heads of both Peter and Paul, he raised them both to the crown of martyrdom; having crucified the one on the wood, and having cut off the head of Paul, leaving to us and to the world the occasion for a festival and such a feast of the passion of the saints. These things, O thrice-blessed ones, the annual law has brought to you, proclaiming everywhere that you are athletes of the common habitation, and improving the minds of men through your honor. For virtue, being honored, raises many to zeal; in Christ Jesus our Lord, to whom belongs the glory and the power, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

Encomium of Asterius, Bishop of Amaseia, to the holy hieromartyr Phocas. The memory of the great things of the saints is good and profitable to those practicing asceticism. For it does not instruct by word alone those desiring virtue and piety, but it also sets forth the actions of those who have lived rightly as manifest teachers. Therefore also our Lord says, giving the pledges of those who have perfected the best: 'Whoever does and teaches, the same shall be called great' (Matt 5:19); and elsewhere: 'Let your light shine before men, so that they may see your good works and glorify your Father in the heavens' (Matt 5:16). For the logical instruction of practical energy is a lesser and weaker teacher; and the more we say that hearing is a more precise vision, the more the practice of the word is judged to hold sway. In this way we learn the skills.

In this way we are trained in skills, first being led by word toward learning, and then grasping the subtle things by hand and by experience. For a geometer, though he does much with the book and has been filled by the hearing of the teacher, will not grasp the power of the various figures unless he learns the points, the lines, and the circles upon the tablet. Nor does the word alone instruct the diligent student desiring the star of law, unless the teacher, having rotated the sphere for him with knowledge, presents the movement of the pole to the eyes. Likewise, a physician who does much according to Hippocrates and the other instructors is an unskilled healer before he has walked among the many sick and learned from them how to heal.

So also we, the disciples of the martyrs, making the actions of patient men our teachers before our own confession, learn to guard piety even unto the most extreme dangers, looking upon their sacred shrines as if they were pillars engraved with letters, clearly declaring the struggle of the testimony. Just as those approaching the oak of Mamre or the fragrant cave, which Ephron the Hittite gave for the burial of Sarah (Genesis 23), where also the patriarch himself lies with the children, immediately renew their imagination through the sight of the places and see with their intellect the faithful patriarch, the firstfruits of piety, and the circumcision in him; and they also consider those who sprang from his root, Isaac and Jacob, and with the memory of the men, the whole history concerning them becomes a spectacle.

In the same way, I today, having grasped the honored tomb of the thrice-blessed Phocas, am filled from the place with the memory of all the narratives told about him; I see the gardener's skill, the unblemished...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Phocas's Hospitality and the Persecution
english: the host

He provided a comfort of life to himself and to those asking. He also opened his small and hardworking table very willingly to strangers. Living by the highway, he prepared what he had in common for those staying there. He was a young Lot, not of the Sodomites, but of Sinope. After some time had passed, he found the commandment was not for nothing; for from hospitality he gained the pretext of the life-giving death; hence, as you heard, having taken a little.

When our word of piety was proclaimed and the majestic announcement went out to every ear, knowing Christ and His mysteries, the nations raged, according to the Psalm, and kings and rulers gathered together for the same purpose; and the peoples of error were enraged at Jesus reigning. Every Christian was sought as an evildoer, and the near one was beaten and the far one was drenched with water.

Therefore, neither the uselessness of the duty nor the gardener hid Phocas, but even he was proclaimed as most genuine of Christ's mysteries. And indeed, the agents of this unhappy and flowing life came upon him, commanded to lead him away unjudged and without defense. For the accusation was such as a bold man shouts out with a bright voice; and without anyone asking, he showed it by his works, and when being inquired into, he shouted out joyfully.

So the agents of his punishment and of our feast came to rest with him, the one being sought, neither knowing nor being known. They had the pretext of the visit in complete secrecy, so that, having first been taught by those outside the city who Phocas was and how he lives, they might stand over him continuously to seize him, just as the Hebrews once in the garden with Judas the Lord.

They came inside having nets holding the prey: the dogs the lamb, the wolves the ram, the doves the snatchers and the thieves; just as the prophet Isaiah says: the hind rested with the leopards, and the lamb grazed with the wolves, and the lions had a common diet with the calf. Since, as he loved to happen, a table and habit of being bold toward one another provided,
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Glory and Utility of the Martyr
english: The martyr inquired of them what kind of men they were and for what reason they had seized his city.

Those who, feeling shame for the prompt reception and hospitality of the man, commanded that nothing spoken be revealed, made known to him the secret thing and the drama being bought out regarding the plot, that they were seeking Phocas for punishment; and by this hospitality, they were worthy to add a favor, to join with them in the hunt for the one sought.

The servant of the Lord heard and, receiving the word with a soul not turned away, suffered nothing lowly or foolish, nor did he counsel to flee the danger out of fear, and having these things, he easily taught the power; but everything contrary, he thought toward the worthiness; 'And I,' he says to you, 'will seize the one lying ahead. For I know the man and, having searched easily, I will report him; and this is not far off, but after one day; only you rest during this meager journey.'

Having thus guaranteed the promise to them firmly, he divided himself into two things: by the reception of his own killers and by the preparation of the tomb. Having arranged the pit and the things necessary for the burial, approaching them at the last, he says, 'With care, I searched for Phocas and the prey is ready; and, if it seems good, let him be seized.' To those saying out of pleasantness, 'And where is the man?', he says, 'Not far, but with you; and this man is for you myself; and use the command and fulfill the purpose of the journey and of the toil.'

The men were struck in their souls and, upon hearing, they marveled at the salt and the table, understanding the host who was ambitious in poverty. He urged toward the daring of the execution and commanded not to hesitate even a little, saying that the murder was not from their hand, but from those who had commanded the work. He said, he persuaded, he suffered; and having his head cut off, he was presented as a priest reconciled to God.
We have this man, men, as a pillar and support of the churches of God until now.

And this most illustrious one is among the best and most blessed, holding the first place. For a star differs from a star in glory, according to common opinion and according to the voice of the vessel of election; and most especially indeed he is most famous among the saints throughout the whole inhabited world.

And he draws all people and runs together toward his own gathering-place; and the thoroughfares from each land are filled with those hastening toward the place of prayer. For that magnificent temple is a relief to the afflicted, a resource to the laboring, a physician to the suffering, and an Egypt to the starving.

And he feeds more abundantly, having finished his life in Phocas, than Joseph did while living; for he indeed distributed grain of silver (Genesis 41), but this one grants wheat to those in need. And just as the doves, during the winter season when food is scarce, find lands with abundant crops and settle in those courts, so do all the poor and the wanderers rush to the isthmus of Sinope as to a common storehouse.

If indeed even elsewhere the martyr established for himself a small deficiency, such as a colony of a metropolis, this place too is wonderful and is looked around at by all Christians, just as this place among us is a sacred gathering-place for those celebrating. For the death of his holy ones is precious before the Lord (Psalm 116:15); and the relics, having been divided many times, preserve the good reputation everywhere in their entirety.

Thus also in the reigning city, the summit of Italy and the queen of the world, there is for him much escort and honor and a magnificent house, arranged for beauty. And the Romans do not treat Phocas with less healing than Peter and Paul. And, as the word teaches, they eagerly took the head of the martyr as a turning away from the defiled Herodias, having determined their purpose. For she, thirsting for blood, sought the head of a righteous man toward insolence; but they made it for honor and for their own benefit. And the sailors and even the ship-owners from everywhere, not only those crossing the Euxine, come here.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The True King and the Vanity of Idols
english: Not a toil, but those cutting across the Adriatic and carried over the Aegean, and all who sail the ocean toward the west and navigate the western gulfs, use the usual commands to rest from the toil of the voyage, turning to a new hypothesis through the euphemism of the brave; and the thrice-blessed is a tongue to them, because it provides clear experiences of help.

Often, however, at night while awaiting winter, a helmsman was seen dozing upon the rudder, waking him; and at other times, stretching a call and attending to the shield and looking out from the prow for the rocks. A law was established for sailors to have Phocaean companions. And since they must have a share in the current incorporeal life helplessly, learn how they wisely reasoned the impossible. Each day, according to the number of those seeing, they complete the portion for the sake of an equal distribution among the eaters, as a testimony.

One of the stewards, driving out the silver, sets it aside, and another the next day, and another at another time; and thus the lot of the purchase, overseeing all, gives the buyer his share each day of the portion. When a harbor receives them and they land upon the earth, the silver is divided among the hungry; and this portion to Phocaeans is a blessing for the needy.

Kings have established this, and they adorn God's palace with the most patient and God-loving and honor-seeking treasures. But those coming upon them love the young more than the elders. And it is no wonder if the men holding the Roman hegemony, being pious and companions to customs and laws, thus act reverently toward the servant of Christ, even when the wonder reached even to the barbarians; and all the wildest Scythians, those who dwell on the opposite shore of the Euxine Sea, inhabitants of Lake Maeotis and the Tanais river, those who dwell in the Bosporus and stretch even to the Phasis river, all these carry spears for the gardener; and all those standing by us in customs and duties toward the...
Only those of one mind become softened in the harshness of their ways by the truth.

One ruler, therefore, having laid aside the crown of his head, being surrounded by gold and flowers of stone, and having stripped off his war-armor—for his panoply was a substance of boastful wealth and was being shattered by the barbarians—sent both offerings through the martyr to God, establishing the occasions of power and dignity. For it was evident, as the crown of kingship was a gift, and the breastplate was the strength for war.

As for the continuous activities occurring through visions in dreams and through the healings which those who labor enjoy, how could anyone even recount them, since it is impossible to apply words to each individual activity? However, it is possible to say this much to those worshipping the manifold error: that one slave of Christ and fellow-slave of ours fulfills the activities of many whom you consider gods among you.

And let the divinations be silent, just as they were hushed by the prophecies among us, the righteous overcoming. Let the works of medicine be idle, and let Asclepius not be worshiped; and let the Dioscuri not be considered to contend with sailors, for most know the Helper against dangers. Where is the Pythia, a woman of false divination, providing oblique and uncertain answers to those inquiring, so that she might prepare an apology for failure and falsehood through the doubt of the oracles? Where is the spring considered to generate prophetic water? Is it not all nonsense and vanity, which lured the wretched peoples toward error?

Worship God, whose faithful slaves were worthy of such grace, not acting involuntarily, but doing good to fellow-slaves according to the gift given to them. And these things [occur] after the arrival here and the separation of the body. Recognize from the servants the majesty of the Lord; glorify the God who is truly above all, to whom worship is due, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Martyrs as Teachers of Endurance
english: It seems that the greatest benefits have been gained even from extremely hostile and unyielding enemies; and this is shown both by the experience of life and by the things being completed perfectly.

For if the devil had not persecuted Christians and waged war against the church, we would not have had martyrs; and if there were no martyrs, our life would have become gloomy and without vigor. For what is comparable to these celebrations? And what is so solemn and beautiful as to see the whole city walking about free from idleness, and occupying a holy place to perform pure mysteries with true piety?

True piety is to worship God and to honor those who, through Him, enduredly withstood sufferings and arrayed themselves against the final danger of death, of whom those who lead us today are the foremost and leaders; men [who became] immortal through a beautiful death, living forever through despising [life], having exchanged the kingdom of blood and having rejected the predatory flesh as a benefactor of the soul.

Thus, a good choice, when it acts like a bridle toward a man, subduing all impulses and movements to itself and, as a bridle holds the reins, keeping the thoughts attentive, softening sluggishness and restraining immeasurable sharpness, is not able to make the course of life disordered or dangerous.

We have, therefore, the martyrs of Christ not only as teachers of a good way of life, but also as accusers of sin. How could an accuser martyr come to be? Listen. If he conquered the flame of fire through endurance, how do you not restrain fornication through temperance? If the martyr did not pity wealth which he was giving away and money, why do you not despise a little silver for the sake of righteousness? If the martyr did not honor the race of God, but shunned woman, children, and dear ones, how do you not slaughter...

Does he, through accidental familiarity with your person, reason away justice and the fear of God as if they were insignificant? If the martyr surrendered his body through God, how can you himself despise a small tunic as if it were a covering for the naked? These things, when examined against one another, expose our own misfortune.

Therefore, should we respect the saints as teachers, or fear them as accusers? Let us show our own lives to those who punish us by following them; and let us ourselves be persuaded by God, just as the saints were persuaded by the commandments and firmly hoped in the promises. For the hope of spiritual goods is a very good teacher of courage and endurance, which, being inherently reliable and a secure earnest deposited in our thoughts, exhorts us to see every danger unshakeable and to bear it bravely in the trial; and this follows accordingly. For by nature we humans are somewhat prone to be softened and to yield to the winds of toil, but to take hold powerfully against them of those things for which contests and honors are the end.

Therefore, all the martyrs, paying attention with their minds to the evangelical letter, in which the Lord, exhorting the holy athletes and those eager for good, says: 'If anyone confesses me before men, I will confess him before my Father' [Matt 10:32], endured iron set against them through irrational thoughts and climbed upon pyres, and providing their bodies to be cast into the mouths of beasts, and each one submitted his back to flogging and the sharp edges of nails, and their sides were scattered, and they endured iron bonds and brought forth dark cries from the dungeons; they were attacked by hunger and thirst and were dried up, and they presented their faces like stones to those striking them, they heard the insolent as if they were deaf, they remained silent toward those insulting and reviling as if they were mute, and they were paraded to the crowds and the theaters.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Glory of Martyrs vs. the Ignorance of Tyrants
english: Marketplaces and stalls were set up in the bodies of those singing praises, not only men but also women, the most wretched of all. Others were scorched by fire, others were struck down by winter; in various ways they divided the excellence among us, so that by falling, they might conquer.

Because of this, having surrounded the pious bodies with reverence—the vessels of election, the instruments of the blessed souls, the dwellings of the philosophers—we guard them as highly precious heirlooms for all life, and we protect them as our own surplus; and for the martyrs, the church is fortified like a city with brave soldiers, and all kinds of festivals are gathered together, and we enjoy the joy of the feasts.

But those being pressed by human circumstances or misfortunes, as if seeking some refuge, hasten to the rest of the thrice-blessed, making themselves ambassadors of their own prayers and requests by means of an exceeding boldness. From here, poverty is released and diseases are healed and the threats of rulers are put to sleep; and for all the disturbances and winters of life, the shrines of the martyrs are prosperous harbors.

Thus a father or mother, having taken up a sick child and having surrounded it with embraces, runs to seek medicine and doctors, but flees to unskilled help; and coming to one of the martyrs, through him she presents the petition to the Lord with such cries used toward the Mediator: 'Intercede through Christ's suffering on behalf of suffering and disease. Having boldness, use your word toward fellow-servants. Even if you left our life behind, you certainly know the sufferings of humanity; you yourself once pleaded before becoming a martyr. When seeking, you received; now having received, grant. Ask for your own gain in the form of old age. May we be healed of our infirmity as the world is of Christ.'

Another, hastening to a marriage, makes the prayer in the martyr-shrines a prelude to the bridal chambers; and someone rushing to a voyage does not first loosen the moorings of the ship, before he invokes the Lord of the sea through the martyrs; and for the poor and the needy, they have gained a common table and food, the rest of the martyrs; and the martyrs are sung of throughout the earth and the sea. Appropriately and according to their worth. For not as many [do] the righteousness [correctly]...

They bore the cross with their own bodies; they did not scatter money, but poured out blood; they did not kill the poor, but did not pity themselves; they did not visit the maltreated in prison, but they themselves wore the chains. Because of this, in exchange for endurance and affliction, they reaped glory and honor.

10.5.1 Thus are the martyrs; but where are those tyrants and murderers, who thought high things and threatened with arrogance, who sit upon lofty thrones and do not know their own ruler? They have leaped over the lions, run over the leopards, fought against the bears, poured out blood against the wolves, and acted wickedly like foxes. More filthy lie the dead donkeys, for oblivion has covered their lives; but they have a tomb that is terrible, a monument of impiety, and a memory of dishonor; they repent in vain, and they groan uselessly.

10.5.2 But the memory of those insulted by them is received by an unceasing remembrance, an ageless praise. For the accounts and the honors, being received by the drunkards from the elders, and grandfathers to grandsons or fathers to children, passing on the healing care for them, make the praise immortal; and just as life preserves these feasts as an inviolable inheritance, or rather something more precious than an inheritance. For indeed, beautiful things of an inheritance are either taken away by a robber, or an enemy takes them as plunder, or a turn of circumstances empties them; but no one shall cut off the feast of holy men from a year, until they are years and time runs and heaven holds the sun and earth grazes its own animals and the sea its exceptional things.

10.5.3 To speak more truly, even when these elements have ceased, though it may seem so to some, the glory of martyrs and righteous ones shall not be extinguished, nor shall that which concerns them be destroyed by the fury of the people; but then they shall blossom even more toward the incorruptible life, once humanity has been re-adorned.

10.6.1 And it is possible for the unbelievers to waver concerning our coming hope, from the things being done in this life, regarding our good expectation of receiving firmly the things laid up. For behold, the whole circle of the inhabited world is filled with the athletes of Christ, and every place holds the memory of the saints; and all times are better than the gifts and growths from the earth, [the things] of the...

title: The distinction between honoring martyrs and worshipping idols
english: Narratives are granted to those celebrating the struggles. As if someone were a devoted friend of the excellent martyrs, and set his care upon celebrating the sufferings of all, not a single day of the year would pass unobserved. For the exploits of brave men possess a glory superior to the solar cycle.

Because the one opposed to the good has attacked the Christian mystery fiercely, and strove to bury all with his own schemes through calamity, and to occupy himself vainly with the tasks of the clay, God, having anointed a multitude of excellent men with commands and trained them for endurance and strength, set them against the shameless and the meddler of humanity. These, moreover, struggled a new kind of struggle. For they did not prevail by striking or smashing, but they excelled by suffering and by being slaughtered.

And what kind of power would you say, listener, is this of war? And what kind of success is this: to be twisted and flogged and, through fire or sword or the cruelty of prisons, to have one's life destroyed? But learn how the wars for piety are made straight from the opposite side of the others. For some have excellence in killing, but others are bloodless in their victory through suffering and falling. And the boldness of the righteous carries out the embassies against the world. And the enemy was caught off guard by the adversaries, whether he fell or intended to. For however many he slaughtered as martyrs, so many helpers of men he prepared.

And in every kind of action, this is found while suffering; therefore, where they think they are obstructing piety, from there they prepare the increase of piety. For the wise God stands against the purposes of the fool and the thoughtless. And we find this following the events of every time: the exposition of Moses and the conduct of Joseph. Immediately in the beginning, the second man murdered Abel (Gen 4:8), so that he might cut off the seed of the pious, and it became fruitful. For from then on, man-slayers are intensely hated, which is why Cain was cursed by God (Gen 4:15). The matter of Christ, that the Satan worked in the Jews so that they might crucify him (Matt 27), is the same. The same thing has happened to the martyrs, whom many despise, trivializing their [life/existence] through their own folly...
A reproach. Is he not a man? Was not the body spent? Is not their memory contained in a few remains and these things? Especially Greeks and Euomians say these things; let us speak to both.

We do not worship martyrs, but honor them as genuine worshippers of God; we do not revere men, but marvel at those who, in the time of trials, have reverently served God well. We place them in beautiful shrines and raise up houses of their rest with magnificent constructions, so that we may emulate the honors of those who well finished their course; and we do not show our zeal for them for pay, but we enjoy their protection toward God.

For our prayer is not sufficient to move God in the time of necessity or misfortune, for our plea is not a persuasion, but a remembrance of sins; therefore we fly to the fellow-servants who are loved by the Lord, so that they might heal our defects through their own achievements. What then is the charge, that while honoring martyrs we ourselves strive to please God? What accusation is there in flying to protectors? Let us examine also these things, if the accuser cleanses the charge. And how [can it be said], that you do not honor myriads of dead men, but worship them as gods?

Did you not, through your folly, deify Demeter and Kore, and yet you honor two women with temples and these sacrifices and with all kinds of worships and healings? Are not the mysteries at Eleusis the essence of your religion, and the Attic people and all Greece flowing together to complete a vanity? Is not the dark descent there, and the solemn gatherings of the hierophant toward the altar, only from woman to woman? Do not the torches go out, and the large and countless people think their salvation to be the things done in the darkness by the two?

Do I say that you worship Dionysus the Theban as a god? For I say, know your fatherland, so that you may know the man: a man, a grape-grower and a vintner, a village leader, a people drawing together and acting shamefully through drunkenness, doing those things which incite the dissolute youths to unchastity, while they drink with the old Silenus and the satyrs who love revelry.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The danger of pride and the legacy of the saints
english: Are you sharing in a life of drunkenness and history? You are not the one offering sacrifices to the man Heracles as if he were a god, but to a Roman man, a body that was lucky and brave, and you revere him because he excelled in many things and became surrounded by beasts.

And again, why do you not revere and have set aside Asclepius, who was in the porch and surrounded by much iron? And you would not deny that you do this. For the temples rising everywhere in the inhabited world—I say the Asclepieia, the Heracleia, and the Dionysia—stand as high indictments of your vanity. And so I shall depart innocent of the reproach, for I do not worship idols nor consider them gods; but you are growing, being held by reproaches, and accusing others of these things, just as those with a guilty conscience accuse the innocent. For you show yourself to be worshipping men as gods. These things are few among the many regarding the pagan.

But you Jews of the new stance, what is wonderful that you dishonor Christ, rejecting the likeness [to the Father], separating [them] in your own words, while guarding the places as sacred, in which holy bodies have rested? But you, who have not come to an understanding of what is happening, fear, you who are called Christians, and yet hate the martyrs along with the Greeks. Do you not know how Christ, the Arch-martyr, first suffered and left zeal to the servants?

Then after him Stephen, the namesake of the orthodox struggle according to God; all the following disciples and apostles. And you have inspected through a single insult how many you dishonor: John the Baptist, James called the brother of the Lord, Peter, Paul, Thomas; these I name as the leaders of the martyrs, and then the infinite multitude of those who died for life. Is it not a small thing for you to stumble over these? Is the danger of your hatred not small?

Each of these conquered the devil with the company of demons, and was inscribed among the angels and is kept as a well-pleasing athlete by the promise of the resurrection; and he shall stand at the appearance of God and our Savior, opening his mouth with boldness, rejoicing in the sight of the angels and in the glory of God, blessing himself for the lashes, the chains, the tortures, the [deformities]...

It is a profit of the end, because of the eternal life he has become a guest. But when you hear these things, I know what you think and say: 'I too am acceptable to my peers. If I live according to virtue, I shall be no worse or less honored than those now admired.' Truly, such words are the mark of a proud man, following the great Pharisee (Luke 18:11) and stranger to all humility. It is evident that he who has not previously been humbled will not ascend to height; for a decision is a master.

To ensure that no one forgives you for becoming such a person—tell me, do you not wish to feel shame before those who cut the path of piety for you, the guides of the good, the teachers of virtue, who trained you in endurance and contempt for death? You were taught gratitude from the disciples of this life, that becoming like those who taught and lacking nothing of the art, they nonetheless love the hearts of the teachers, respect them, speak well of them, yield to the first ones, and serve them as a father.

Many also, having ended their lives, holy saints are able, even after departing from life, to do good to men; and witness to these things is Elisha, who long ago, having departed from life and fallen asleep, but having received the grace of God immortal and inseparable, was present in the earth and with the lifeless bones (2 Kings 13:21). For you know, as a lover of the Scriptures and a disciple, that someone dead, being carried out by his own people, perhaps being seized by robbers or enemies, such as it is pleasing to happen in commotion and noise, having been thrown upon the tomb of the thrice-blessed prophet, was immediately revived and rose to the living.

What then shall we say regarding what happened? Did the righteous man have no perception of what was being done? Did he not send up a prayer for the dead as for the child of the woman of Samos? But the truth of things gives us nothing of the sort to conceive. For the righteous man lay there long ago, the body having been dissolved into kindred soil and like dust. But it has become evident that God, always glorifying His own people even after their end, performs wondrous paradoxes concerning their tombs and their resting places, so that the living, always having a more intoxicating hold on the good hope, may hold onto those who have departed.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Value of the Righteous
english: They willingly sacrifice their lives for the honor of the best political order.

Likewise, for Elijah, the one who guided this prophet with the flaming horses and the fiery chariot, living in another kind of life and having departed from men to the place he received, he left a symbol sufficient of his own power, even the mantle. Yet what was the value of that thing? For it was nothing other than a dead and trivial skin from old age. However, even the Jordan itself yielded to it, and the water was split and stood divided, just as the old [Jordan] was before Jesus, who was a type of what was to come (2 Kings 2:11).

The Theban [Elisha] also was present, and he received the garment of the philosopher as a disciple, making the crossing of the river secure, honoring the philanthropy of God and the garments of the saints as if they were endowed with soul. And so that it might be clearly shown that the miracle concerning the river did not happen because of the cause of the water being struck, but because of the honor of the one inhabited and taken up, Elisha's water was struck, and the water flowed normally, nothing new having suffered. And since, having failed, he cried out: 'Where is the God of Elijah?' (2 Kings 2:14), and having cried out a second time, he sat down, immediately the river, splitting the stream, showed the dry land, and the prophet, having trodden, arrived at the other side.

And Joseph, after Jacob had died, not loving him as a father so privately, but honoring him as a common patriarch of the nation, with that much-celebrated service, led the remains out of Egypt, so as to allow Moses, after the writing of the world's genesis and the rest of the history, to give this also as a narrative of life. And Joseph again was present with the Israelite departing from the eyes, as one might say, stolen from Pharaoh, and the body was everywhere present with the people, and he led it with care as a good and evil-averting secure safeguard for the sixty myriads.

And they had such reverence regarding the ark of the forefather, as regarding the holy ark which bore the law of God. Therefore also David, entreating God to be propitious and favorable to the people, and exhausting him with myriads of supplications, so that having stilled the continuous and recurring plague of misfortunes, he might again govern Jerusalem with good foresight as before, thus says: 'O Shepherd of Israel, pay attention, O Leader of Joseph like a sheep' (Ps 80:2). For he is appeased by the names of the beloved and friends, and most gracefully handles the entreaty of the transgressing multitude of sins, as if concealing and covering them with the titles of the holy fathers.

This is told to our mind by the word concerning the saving of Sodom (Gen 18-19). For Abraham, entreating the Sodomites, when God, after foretelling, brought the punishment upon them as they were displeased, the sparing of the righteous being worthy to save the whole people. For beginning from the fifty toward the ten, he concluded, and God immediately granted the entreaty, as if weighing on some scale and weights, opposing the value of the ten righteous against the myriads of sinners.

In order that it might be shown more abundantly to us all, that even one righteous person is a precious thing and a friend to God, since the tenth failed to be a number and the multitude of the holy was found suffering from the smallness of the sinners, and it was necessary for the law-breakers to receive the penalty of audacity; Lot is violently driven from the condemned places and is saved entirely into the old age of his own righteousness, having received all his household from God (Gen 19). Therefore, a righteous person is a great possession: first, a benefit to himself; second, a lasting treasure to the rest of his race, unknown to sight and always accompanying them, silent and instructing others by his deeds; lying of old and living by his good repute. Good for the children.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Intercession of the Wise and the Fall of Solomon
english: It is an inheritance and an asylum, which time does not consume and a robber does not take away. For it is incorporeal and without body, trading among incorporeal souls.

You see how even the glorious and the un-songworthy Israelites, being deprived of all things and cast out from the land, were not deprived of or stripped of the title of being called from the God-loving forefather; but even while serving barbarians, they were freed because of the righteousness of the fathers, and while living in the desert, they were nourished because of the good reputation of those born; and though sinning continually and blaspheming many times, and being worthy of the destroying punishment, they were made worthy because of the merciful Abraham, and because of Israel they obtained forgiveness, impudent children being saved by the old age of the fathers.

And you know, O lover of learning, how at first when God called Moses from the shepherdship to the leadership of the peoples, He immediately says these things to the servant: 'I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob' (Exodus 3:6). And having become a little person of the Word, He adds these: 'Gather the assembly of the sons of Israel and say to them: The Lord, the God of your fathers, appeared to me, the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob' (Exodus 3:16).

And thus in preambles, God seals the descendants with the name of the righteous fathers, like a certain sign, knowing it to be good and profitable to be known from them. But after time had passed, when the people turned toward insolence against the Benefactor and despised the Savior, and they applied themselves to the idol-making of the calf and worshiped a lifeless skull, having lost the living and rational intellect,
Moses, not having such things as these to appease the Master on behalf of the disciples, the much-toiling pedagogue flees to the memory of the fathers and with them the entreaty...

It is cast, he says, in this way: having remembered Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the saved ones, before whom you swore to yourself that their seed would multiply like the stars of heaven (Genesis 22:17).

Great is the wrath and the fury, and it is unavoidable; but the wise and resourceful petitioner, having surrounded himself with the countenances of the saints and having cast down to God the cities of the elders through their memory, extinguished the punishment like a flame, healing the wounds with the paternal oil of those who remain.

Leaving the Mosaic book, he moved on to the books of the Kings. For there also he is seen worthy of pity, because he was the offspring of a God-loving father. And this is Solomon, the one of many thrones; who, since as time went on he was not a ruler of sufferings, but rather a slave and more uncontrolled in the flesh, and because of the heedlessness of life, he changed and subverted the ancestral piety, shaping idols that are stumbling blocks to the law.

God says to him: 'I will tear your kingdom apart and give it to your servant; however, in your days I will not do this because of David your father; from the hand of your son I will receive it' (1 Kings 12:9). These things instruct us through history; and the song of the Psalms teaches similar things: 'I was young; and indeed I have grown old, and I have not seen a righteous man left abandoned, nor his seed seeking bread' (Psalm 37:25).

But, as it seems, when once the soul of truth is shattered and it has rushed headlong into innovating instead of living in order, nothing is able to turn it back to the straight and ordered way; but resisting the bridle, just as a stubborn donkey is led toward the pit, overcoming the rider in mind by the impulse toward evil, such is it to see these Eunomians also.
For thus these men love to be called men rather than of Christ, blaspheming God and dishonoring the men of God, but rather...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Honor of Martyrs and Introduction to Euphemia
english: Whether they are being awed by the resting places of the saints, or are acting with prudence toward the altars and the defiled places. The ascetics of that deprivation and those who consider the terror against all things to be virtue thought that the shouts of the demons would be ashamed of the bright power of the martyrs crying out and shouting, and of those calling each one by name as if present, and driving away and chasing the oppressed humans.

Whether one wishes to say that the spirits of the athletes of piety act against the unclean spirits, or that angels attend the holy tombs in honor of those who have rested, it makes no difference; for whatever is said, it is the glory of those who suffered for the love toward Christ. The benefits of the martyrs appear manifest every day, sometimes in different and diverse ways, which free the wanderers from the operations of the satanic. For those who were once seized by madness and held by evils are now seen to be acting with prudence, and we see the boldness of the embassy of the saints testifying to the facts.

And just as unmistakable proofs of the power of our Savior were contained in the midst of the Hebrews—those cleansed of leprosy, those whose sight was healed, the blind, and if any paralytic, having been strengthened in the harmony of his limbs, walked without hindrance—so also now those who carry the cross for the sake of Him who was crucified provide clear proofs by the grace of the Lord, healing the faithful in various and diverse ways like fellow-slaves.

And Paul and Peter—the one having expelled the Python demon (Acts 16:18), the other having raised the lame man at the temple gates (Acts 3:6)—turned Hebrews and Greeks toward obedience to the gospel through practical powers; but the evil assembly of heretics now badly harasses our...

The martyrs are not respected even for the greatness of the miracles. Instead, people call them many-maned, and their tombs and their resting places are named as such, and they cleanse themselves as if rubbing against a contagion, not even mentioning that God-breathed saying praised by every mouth: 'Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His saints' (Psalm 116:15). Therefore, let us pray to God, and let us entreat the martyrs to revile the Lord in common, so that a spirit of compunction may be given to those acting under the error of heresy, and the division may be loosed like a mediator or a barrier, so that all may come together in brotherly unity in Christ Jesus our Lord, to whom belongs the glory forever. Amen.

The discourse of Asterius, Bishop of Amaseia, concerning the holy Euphemia the martyr.
