First, O men, I had Demosthenes in my hands, the formidable one, and those Demosthenian things where Aeschines strikes bitterly at the memories; having been stained by the word and having thickened the intellect, I was in need of relaxation and a walk, so that the suffering of my soul might be somewhat released. Having come out of the room and having conversed a little with acquaintances in the marketplace, from there I arrived at the temple of God to pray at leisure.

As I happened to do this and was walking one of the covered walkways, I saw a certain painting there and the sight seized me intensely: you would say it was a work of Euphranor or one of those ancients who, having taken up the art of painting, worked great lifelike panels with little effort. Come here, for if you wish for a leisure narrative now, I will describe the painting to you; for we do not have medicines from the children of the Muses that are any less inferior than those of the painters. A certain woman, a holy virgin, having consecrated her chastity to God, they call Euphemia; and when a tyrant was once driving away the pious, she eagerly sought death.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Artist's Depiction of the Passion
english: Danger; but the citizens and sharers in the religion for which she died, having marveled together at her courage and the sacredness of the virgin, having placed the shrine near the temple and laid down the casket, perform honors to her and make the annual feast a common and widespread celebration, a panegyris.

Therefore, the celebrants of the mysteries of God always honor the memory by word and by intention, and they teach the associated people with care how she completed the contest of endurance. And the painter himself, through his art, having engraved with all possible power the whole history upon linen, placed before the shrine a sacred spectacle; and here is the artistic skill.

A judge sits high upon a throne, looking bitterly and with hostility at the virgin; for he is angry whenever the art [seeks] even with soulless materials. And there are spear-bearers of the ruler and many soldiers; some carrying the tablets of the memoranda and styluses, one of whom, having raised his hand from the wax, looks intensely at the one being judged, turning his whole face, as if rising to intercede, speaking so that she might not write incorrectly or errantly concerning the hearing, being weary.

And the virgin stands in a purple tunic and robe, signifying philosophy, as it seemed to the writer, and her appearance is charming, as it seems to me, the soul having been beautified by virtues. And two soldiers lead her toward the ruler, one pulling her by the face, the other hurrying from behind. The appearance of the virgin is gripped by modesty and severity; for she indeed bows toward the earth as if reddening the faces of the men, but she stands unshakeable, suffering nothing in the cowardly contest.
If I had previously praised other painters, I would have beheld the drama of that woman of Colchis, as she is about to bring to the children the...

A sword divides the face with mercy and anger; one of the eyes manifests wrath, while the other manifests the mother being pitied and trembling. Now I have shifted the wonder of the Scripture from that idea to this one; and I am most ignorant of the artist, because he has rather mixed the bloom of colors, combining shame and courage together, through natural sufferings.

Moving forward into the face of the imitation, certain criminals in small tunics, already naked, were beginning the work; and the one, seizing the head and leaning it toward the back, provided for the other a suitable position for the punishment of the virgin's face; and the assistant was cutting out the pearly teeth; and a hammer and a chisel appear as the instruments of the punishment. My eyes weep from here, and the passion strikes my speech; for the painter has colored the drops of blood so vividly that you might say they are truly flowing from the lips, and you would depart mourning.

After these things, a prison; and again the solemn virgin sits alone in light-colored garments, stretching out her hands toward heaven and calling upon God, the helper of the distressed. While she prays, the sign appears above her head, which indeed the law commands Christians to worship and to inscribe, a symbol I think of the passion which was receiving her.

Immediately, indeed, and after a little while, the painter kindled a fierce fire elsewhere, making the flame by applying red color here and there. He stands her in the middle, having spread her hands toward heaven, showing no pain in her face, but on the contrary rejoicing because she has emigrated to the incorporeal and blessed life.

Up to this point the painter has set his hand and I too my speech; it is time for you, if you wish, to finish the Scripture, so that you may understand accurately, lest we have come much after the explanation.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Glory of the Disciples
english: How truly holy and beautiful is the circle of things that gladden us! For a feast succeeds a feast and a festival seizes a festival; and we are called from prayer to prayer, and the honor of the servant seizes the divine manifestations of the Lord.

Even if regarding his birth, one might be indifferent to him who was born yesterday through flesh and is always existing according to divinity, and even regarding his martyrdom, which the brave one underwent today, one will find many diverse things, but one purpose: that we might be taught piety.

Yesterday, therefore, we learned through the cyclical and customary feast that the Savior of the world was born, and the incorporeal clothed himself in flesh, and the bodiless put on a body; then that he also accepted sufferings on our behalf and was lifted up on the wood not for anyone else's sake but for our salvation. Today, however, we see the brave combatant being stoned for that sake, so that by blood he might repay the debt for the sake of the love which is above blood.

Stephen, therefore, the gatherer of this festival, who calls us to the joy we behold, who led the people as one city, a man the firstfruit of the martyrs, a teacher of the sufferings for Christ, a foundation of the good confession. For before Stephen, no one poured out blood for the sake of the Gospel.

But just as that Cain, the brother-slayer, as the history of Moses teaches me regarding brother-slaying (Genesis 4), committed the act—for having taken strife instead of natural friendship, he first defiled the earth with murder—so also Stephen, the thrice-blessed, first sanctified the earth with the blood of his own, through the combats of the pious, a man second to the times of the apostles, but first in his courageous deeds.
And do not be indignant with me, Peter; do not be grieved, James; do not be harsh, John, if I do not only compare this man to your philosophy, but if I wish to grant him something even more.

Rather, be ashamed, for you are deficient fathers, and you exult in the achievements of the sons and are pleased to be surpassed by the children in virtue. For if anything is beautiful and great regarding Stephen, this is certainly yours, as those who instructed and initiated him.

For the approval of the athletes becomes the glory of the trainer. Therefore, having asked you for a small concession, I will speak with boldness, as the subject gives to me for the sake of advocating what is best concerning Christ. You are an elder of the disciples, holy Peter, and before all things you proclaimed Jesus Christ. Furthermore, while you were preaching your evangelical word, going from city to city and from land to land without ceasing and laboring in the preaching, this one, having entered the stadium and having snatched the crown from the competitors, having gone into heaven, was glorified while you were still turning about the earth; and the greater [glory] is of his Father and Son calling him through the wonderful vision. Thus indeed [it is with] Peter, and what has been said is sufficient. For it is daring to contend with the fathers much more concerning precedence.

Let us also see the others, James, brother of John. You are an evangelist of Christ, a second prize after Peter. And who would not praise your faith? For you were only called and, intending nothing else, you obeyed. You left behind the boat and the father Zebedee; and you followed Christ as a genuine disciple. You suffered willingly for the sake of piety, I confess; for Herod the tyrant used you with the sword (Acts 12:2), but after Stephen, many years later.

And why do I name them one by one, when when the prize of martyrdom was lifted up for all the saints together, first setting oneself against the devil and first conquering, imitating David, even if through a reversal of the matter? David conquered Goliath with stones (1 Samuel 17), and Stephen conquered the devil with stones; but the one with what he threw, and the other with what he was struck by. We, however, the people of Christ, as the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Courage of Stephen
english: Then we cry out with the army of Israel and sing victory songs as if seeing them present, marveling as if they were standing.

For every one who fights for piety is good, even if he becomes second or third to those who competed before; yet he is not worthy of such a marvel as the first. The second, being stirred by zeal for the one who preceded, was thus drawn toward diligence; but he who uses no one as a guide, yet having become a discoverer of the good, appropriately receives the vote of the first.

Great indeed is the man's readiness, therefore great is the honor; and immortal is the memory, which neither oblivion covered nor time dimmed, but generation after generation, inheriting the stories, we priests, people, children, men, and women, celebrate this feast without fail. But the history itself should also be observed, so that, having become acquainted with the facts of the matters, we might more marvel at the man.

First among those who serve according to Christ was Stephen, esteemed by grace, a vessel filled with the Spirit, confirming daily those in the household and those wandering toward the straight path. And because he had a more intense teaching, he more than the other apostles loosed the enemies and, before them, first made the devil hostile. For he sets his eyes like fire and looks fiercely at those who are more steadfast in piety. Thus the race of Alexandrians raised up a sharp-edged system against him for a stand. In any case, you have heard of the men of the city, how they are both fervent and boiling upon everything they might readily rush toward. And when the crowd saw those rushing toward him, it had almost been possible to set the present situation aside; however, he found a resourceful, well-composed, and gentle word. For there is no medicine of such a kind for the healing of temper and agitation, such as a pleasant and well-fitted exhortation.

And 'tell me,' he says, 'the cause of the hatred, instead of why you stretch out your hands and are manifest as if about to strike.' When it was said that 'Since you destroy the ancestral laws and are an introducer of foreign dogmas,' the blessed one stood in the midst; for as an unskilled and impromptu orator, he was saying what he had learned from art, but what was breathed into him by the Spirit: 'Men,' he says, 'brothers and fathers.'

Listen. The introduction is wise, an excellent thing for the people being warmed by it, the beginning of the oration. For the sweetness and the appropriateness of the words, as if participating in some honey or soft oil, diminished the heat of the beasts. Then he rises in memory toward Abraham, so that having begun from ancient times and stretching out a long discourse in much of the middle, he might not be found to have spent his spirit being exhausted. And having worked out that much speech, he shows that even Moses prophesied Christ, so that through the reliability of the lawgiver, skillfully, like a thief, he might introduce the word of faith. And he has said all things knowing, all that was useful for the benefit of those listening.

But when he saw the evil to be unprovable and the opinion unyielding, then he was filled with boldness and, forbidding all the flattering art toward the life here, he unhesitatingly reproved them: stiff-necked, uncircumcised in heart, fighting against the law, warring against the Spirit. And what [things] from here? Many dogs and fattened bulls stood around him as a Master, as the psalmody says, surrounding the righteous man (Psalm 22:2). But he stood alone, surrounded on every side by the people of the murderers. And no one was near at that hour, no friend, no householder, no relative. For it is as if one offers a consolation to those in danger by seeing someone known nearby.

But the high champion of the great struggle, having seen the need for a man to stand by, for he was very brave, shows that he suffered all human things unceasingly; as it seems to him, gazing intently toward heaven (Acts 7:55), he shows also the Son standing at the right hand in the form of humanity (Acts 7:56). O, the philanthropy! O, the goodness! To the athlete, those for which he struggled appeared, and the God of all things did not leave such a voice to him alone. Do not suffer anything ungentle, O Stephen; you have no human ally, no friend stood by you in the time of terrors, but I, with the Beloved, watch over the things being done. Rest is ready, the gates of paradise having been opened. Having endured a little, leave behind a brief life and hasten toward the life which is eternal and perfect. Still finding yourself in the flesh, you see God, a thing of all the world.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Martyrdom and Prayer of Christ-bearer
english: You were initiated by the more prominent apostles into the truth that the Father has a genuine, beloved Son. I show myself to you so that you may be able to bear the burden. And the Son stood by my side, so that you might know his honor by the relation of place. At that time, many were scandalized that God had clothed himself in flesh on earth; but see him now in the heights, with me, bearing the form of man in the heavenly and hyper-heavenly realms, as a confirmation of the completed economy. Do not be crushed or grow limp by being overwhelmed by this.

Looking at the athlete, do not be afraid of the contest. Do not despise the body, treating it as an earthly bond, a fragile house, or a corrupt vessel of a potter. Ascend toward the end here in freedom, for the crown of manliness is ready for you. Transfer from the earth to heaven. Leave the body to the scavengers like food for dogs. Leave behind a raging people and come to the dance of angels.

After this resolve, God appeared to the patient one, so that he might not suffer something cowardly, and might release much eagerness through the greatness of fear. Therefore, God neither sent him an angel as a helper, as he later did for the apostles in prison (Acts 12:5), nor any ministerial and fellow-servant power, but he manifested himself. For it was then the firstfruits of the testimony, and it was necessary for the first work to be completed, so that those following, being built up as witnesses, might receive a strong foundation of zeal and not become imitators of cowardice, which is exactly what happens in common wars. For one soldier, a champion, providing the glorious part of the work, having conquered and having emboldened all his own, strikes down the opponents; yet, having suffered a slight injury, he immediately collapses and fills the souls of his kinsmen with cowardice, and flight becomes a habit. For this reason, God appeared from heaven.

But he who was worthy of the great vision did not hold in silence what he saw, but immediately cried out: 'Behold, I see the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God!' (Rev 4:1). For he thought that the revealing of the vision would draw the unbelievers into agreement. But those making the spoken word a starting point for greater wrath and madness, attempting to block...

They held their ears against the word as if it were blasphemy, immediately ready for death. Dragging the Christ-bearing man outside the city, bearing his endurance as the Lord bore the cross, they return evil for evil and justify murder with murder, and with stones they bind the one who serves the cornerstone.

Standing him on a certain level field, that long body and high trophy of the martyrs, the mob of blood and wrath surrounded him, and imitating the sling used in wars, they threw stones at the servant of the cornerstone, and every Hebrew hand enacted the murder; the aim was for those leaving that the martyr stood in the middle like a target for an archer.

As the body was shattered from every side and smeared with blood, it rushed toward the upright position; it leaned and threatened to fall like a tall plane tree being worked on by many carpenters; but it did not suffer an improper fall according to the many. For it was not cast headlong, nor was it thrown on its side, nor was the form reclined upon its back, but having set its knees in the proper form of one praying, it descended, hastening with the soul through prayer the separation from the flesh and crying out to the visible Lord: 'Lord Jesus Christ, receive my spirit.'

For he was hastening as if to some migration, as if from a foreign land to a fatherland, as if to a bright city from a desert and smoky land. And he added to his petition the prayer for those throwing stones. For those blessing and those stoning were saving, and those murdering were making alive, and those separating from the clay were sending to the kingdom.

Let us therefore consider also the word of the prayer, regarding toward what end it carries 'Lord, do not hold their sin against them' (Luke 23:34). For it is not, as some wickedly thinking men suppose, that the sin of the enemies becomes unpunished and unaccountable. For this was clearly to stand against God's decree and to restore the judgment and law of the righteous, having completed what was due to the murderers.
But what does he say? 'Lord, do not hold their sin against them,' that is: Give the fear of compunction, lead to repentance those now having dared,
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Presence of the Spirit in Stephen
english: Do not allow yourself to die in circumcision; draw through repentance toward your own recognition, and kindle in the hearts the flame of the Spirit. For if they are improved in this way, it is evident that you will not stand against their sin, but having washed in the bath of grace, both your blood and mine, they will become free from the accusations.

These things happened and the drama was completed. And the armies of angels were rejoicing in the contest, marveling greatly and with much retinue leading Stephen into his own inheritance; but the devil was turned away empty, being terribly perplexed, but in order to imitate a prophetic word concerning the airy spirit, saying something more bodily, as one carrying the face of a pot as a vessel and, on the contrary to what he expected, having succeeded in those by which he thought to diminish Christians, through those he increased the list of the martyrs.

And what also toward Paul is the temple? For he too was one of the murderers, a true Benjamin, a wolf having snatched the lamb. For if he himself did not stone, but kept the garments of those stoning and served the people's crowd. Moreover, I shall see you soon, now trembling and breathing a wild passion like a weak old woman being led about, when you are about to be led toward the Ananias of the truth, having tasted it.

And I shall laugh very much when I hear you recounting your tribulations for the sake of the gospel and, among the other dangers, saying: 'At last I was stoned.' For it is necessary for you to defend yourself through stones against the stones, and by the same suffering to loose the accusation of sin.

It is also unbearable not to leave the vision of Stephen behind; for the God of all things always, foreseeing what is about to happen to the lives of sinful men, provides the remedy defensively in advance, which indeed He has done even here. For if the theophanies were completed only for the benefit of the combatant, it would have sufficed to become a voice from the heavens, just as at the baptism before, or later at the transfiguration, or even as with this Paul, when he was traveling toward Damascus.
Now, because the evil from Libya is about to lie in wait for the churches of God, and the ill-famed confusion of the hypotheses...

To lead into life, for this reason God, as if cutting ahead in advance and securing the souls of those who are to come later, shows himself to Stephen in a private and self-sufficient glory, and shows the Son in a perfected appearance, and places him at his own right hand, so that through the clarity of the persons he might interpret the underlying realities.

12.13.1 And someone might happen to say: The things concerning the Father and the Son are thus philosophized for you, but where is the Holy Spirit? For if, for the sake of the security according to faith, the Father was appearing from heaven with the Son, it was necessary for the Holy Spirit also to be present, so that some practical initiation might be accomplished for men through the vision. It is therefore necessary to say to the mind bearing this against us: O most wise, the examiner of readers must have both a correct mind and a strengthened memory, so that he may be able thus to run through all the written things together.

12.13.2 For if you also seek the presence of the Spirit, become a little higher than the stones and the marble, and you will find before the vision the Spirit speaking and being present with Stephen and preparing the athlete. For immediately at the beginning of the narrative he pre-announced this voice to us: 'Stephen, full of grace and truth, was doing signs and great wonders among the people' (Acts 6:8). And some rose up from the assembly called the Libertines and the Cyrenians and the Alexandrians and those from Cilicia and Asia, disputing with Stephen, and they were not able to withstand the wisdom and the spirit with which he was speaking (Acts 6:9-10).

12.13.3 Behold, then, also the person of the Spirit has been made clear to us by the word. If this was written earlier, and the Father and the Son last, the faith is not deprived of anything regarding the order. For it is the custom of the Scripture to do this: sometimes naming the Son alone, sometimes the Spirit with the Son, or sometimes beginning from the Father and concluding in the Spirit; and the repetition of the beginning occurring from the Spirit through the Son, the word leads back to the Father.
12.13.4 And this idiom of custom is seen to be happening most without concealment by the great Paul. And it has been filled among us
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Sharing Justice and the Danger of Harsh Judgment
english: And to Stephen the duty; if one looks toward the magnitude, [it is] not sufficiently, but if toward the power of the one saying, it is sufficient: that to our God is the glory unto the ages of the ages. Amen.

A Pharisee man, as we recently heard Luke saying (Luke 7:36), invites the Lord to a meal and leads Him to a dining room and sets a common table. But he neither declines the invitation nor flees the man, whether being a disciple or having believed, yet being bound to the letter of the law and not yet having opened the eyes toward the knowledge of the truth, and being made dull toward the promises of the prophets.

What then has Luke written this summary for us (Luke 1:1-4)? Whether so that we may have the knowledge of what Jesus accomplished living in the body, and receive useful knowledge of history? Or that a certain useful and educational thought fills our life, regulating it toward the right and the incorruptible? Thus, I think it is good to have, and it is fitting for you to be persuaded.

For many are those justifying themselves, self-loving and self-sufficient, swollen in presumption through empty wisdom, calling sinners those who approach, and before the true criterion comes, separating themselves like lambs from the shouting ones and looking toward the door of the kingdom as if it were about to fall to them, not being worthy to share with the many in a roof or in bindings, but loathing all those who walk not the extreme, but the middle path of life.

Therefore Luke, the physician of more souls than bodies, wrote the narrative in hand not merely as a word, but as a medicine for those sick with self-will, showing Him, our God and Savior, the incomparably pure and only righteous, most compassionately associating Himself with those who are recognized [as sinners] and with those who not yet...

Sharing with those who have been purified, not in order to take on their wickedness, but in order to impart one's own righteousness, according to this solar energy which appears, so as to present the providence of the Creator to the creation.

For we know that the sun does not only illuminate the elevated regions, but also as many places as are deeper and lower than the human position. Let us therefore cease if any of us think in such a way as the Word says; but let us imitate the merciful and man-loving nature of the Master by descending to the lowly, not so that we might humble ourselves to those who are lowly, but so that we might lift them up, just as certain swimmers lift up those who are drowning toward this life-giving air.

Since the Gospel letter leads toward a noble thought, let us stretch ourselves toward the intended goal. I wonder greatly at those who are surrounded by this passion and love of flesh, yet are defeated each day by sleep and the stomach—and indeed, not only having an endless supply of other provocations common to all of us who share the same and one nature—how they are such harsh judges of those who sin, while being so forgiving of themselves; they are weak combatants and unnecessary lawmakers, as if to deny hope in the philanthropy of God and to block, as they suppose, the abundant source of mercy and, with much authority, to bar the entrance to the Kingdom from those who wander. This is nothing like divine economy, but brings misunderstanding to souls seeking healing. For the slave who has lost hope in the cure becomes entirely a stranger to the disease and to every promise of our Scriptures; for even to the one examining such things wisely, nothing is granted except by grace and healed by forgiveness. And who is so sarcastic and disobedient to the words of Job, shouting out to everyone that...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Mercy of the Divine Judge
english: No one is clean from filth, nor even for one day is his life. And who, being sensible, would think such a thing, as being subject to these same accounts in the court of God, to consider forgiveness superfluous and mercy useless?

If indeed they had run toward the very edge of justice and exactness, having truly trodden according to what is written upon the serpent and the scorpion (Gen 3:1), and having been proclaimed victors and crowned against sin, it was not so that they should regulate life toward their own courage and toward all other things, but rather to confess the grace to the Giver God for their own good-pleasing, that they had also masterfully controlled their nature and had not become handlings of satanic temptations, but to reach out with brotherly love toward those who have grown weak, and to raise them up from the mire and cleanse them from the pollutions.

For those receiving honors would thus have taken double praise, of their both their own manliness and of brotherly and good sympathy. But now, being humans who fall to the ground and living a life not the angelic one and near the incorporeal ones, but such as if anyone were to lead and judge by accounts, they judge strictly and with much of the authority that brings a condemning vote, as if to say of me, often being suffocated by the dust and by arrogance, I would speak the evangelical sayings against them, that not seeing the views of others through the eyes you suppose in your own, you remove the splinters (Matt 7:3-5). And binding the heaviest burdens to others, you bypass, heavy judges and weak burden-bearers, seizing the step of Christ and snatching away the decision of the Judge, contemptible slaves and unnecessary judges of fellow-slaves.

If you zeal for God as having been created according to an image, imitate the archetype yourselves; O Christians, the Philanthropic name, zeal for the love of Christ, and turn toward the wealth of his philanthropy. For, intending to appear to men through a man, he preordained John, the preacher of repentance (Luke 3:3), the introducer of regret, and all before John as teachers of turning, the prophets. Then also he himself, having appeared after a little time, cries with his own voice personally: 'Come to me, all you who labor and are burdened, and I will give you rest (Matt 11:28).'

How did he respond when persuaded by the call? He gave a remission of sins without cost, and a release from those who grieve that is uncalculated and brief. The Word sanctified, the Spirit sealed; the old man was buried by the water, the new man was born rising by grace.

What follows? A man becomes his own instead of an alien, a son instead of a stranger, a mystic out of the profane, a holy one out of the ungodly. Therefore, having been enriched by such magnificent and unsurpassed gifts, if one, sinning against the ambitious and good benefactor, were not immediately mindful of the word before you difficult and negligent judges, he would certainly be driven to destruction, being cut off from this life and being punished there.

But since another is the Lord of the verdict, who makes mercy into thousands and myriads and does not wish the death of the sinner, but awaits the return, even so those who insulted the former grace were not punished; rather, a second mercy follows the first, and forgiveness is joined with amnesty. A tear falling is equal to the washing, and a groan over toil brings back the grace that had withdrawn a little.

If you do not believe the word, ask Peter, sitting in the house of the high priest, and he will tell you how, bitterly mourning the lapse of his denial, he was cleansed, and he did not dissolve into Simon, but Peter remained the apostle.

I myself think that even Judas Iscariot, if he had quickly become his own executioner, judging his sin unpardonably and falling down to ask mercy, would not have missed the mercies that overflow throughout the inhabited world. The proof of this word is all the Hebrews who, after the cross, believed, washing their souls and their hands together in the washing. If those who crucified were shown mercy, how could the betrayer not have escaped the amnesty?

Paul also once bound Christians, but having later borne the chains for Christ, he released the complaints from his own passion; he sinned while stoning Stephen and consenting to the killers, but having been stoned, he wiped out the multitude. Matthew and Zacchaeus once were tax collectors, but having trodden upon the tax office through contempt for things, the one received Jesus in his house and more in his soul, the other [received] the works of wonders.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Mercy and the Judgment of God
english: He was shown to be an evangelist and a writer. The tax collector who was with the Pharisee is necessary for remembrance; likewise the woman who lost the drachma and found it (Luke 18:10; Luke 15:8).

But from beginning to end, if anyone were to consider the men of all life in their respective times, he would find many first entangled in sins, then having been moved by a slight inclination toward the better, having established a purpose. For it is the property of God alone to set everything right without any deficiency. But man, being driven by generation and corruption and being subject to so many things, could never be shown to be blameless through the cutting away of forgiveness.

Look toward David the king of Israel, whom God chose by election, and who adorned himself with praises through testimony, saying: 'I have found a man after my own heart, David the son of Jesse' (Acts 13:22). This man, after that brilliant exaltation of praises, because he was seized by the passion of carnality and fell into those things which we all know, yet after the rebuke of the prophet, he came to a calculation of the evil, and left a written record for those looking toward repentance in the future regarding the toil.

And we behold, as in an image, in the Psalter, the man: now being gripped by sorrow in the body, and then making time for weeping in the night, the common rest from pains; and flowing with tears upon the bed as if from the springs of the eyelids, and again to us having labored out the fiftieth psalm (Psalm 50), a type of one propitiating God. Not was the lamentation produced in vain for him, but the heavy groans drew in mercy, and he received both the authority of the royal power and the boldness of supplication toward God.

Similarly, he who had the lot of ruling Nineveh was accompanied by the multitude of sins toward destruction together with the peoples beginning to perish (Jonah 3), and he proclaimed the rebuke of sin approaching with little time left for the punishment. But since they, having sensibly wronged themselves, fled the trial of the calamity, he was grieved that the prophet of evils did not relent, and he became harshly angry toward the mercy of God.
And he who, everywhere both through words and deeds, makes known to us how much favor he has toward men, nurtures the gourd over the head for the...

The ray of the sun provides a covering for the vegetable that is withering, yet the shadow, failing to provide continuous protection, dries it up. Then, as if struggling to wake up to what is happening, it [the person] reproaches and blames. If one so passionately grieves over a withered vegetable, would God not be moved by a city approaching such danger? Learn, then, you harsh and unmerciful ones, the goodness of Him who created us, and do not become bitter and heavy-handed judges among fellow slaves, until He who reveals the secrets of hearts arrives to distribute the state of the expected life to each according to their lot by His sovereign authority. Do not issue your decisions in secret, so that you may not be subjected to the same, and walk as if pierced by the words of your own people as if they were sharp. For it seems to me that even the Gospel forewarning of this serves as a safeguard, saying: 'Do not judge, so that you may not be judged' (Matthew 7:1). For it does not cast out judgment and good-knowledge, but names the harshest condemnation 'judgment.' Therefore, if you wish, make the scale light, if you do not want to be dragged down by the condemning tablet and your own deeds when our life is being weighed in the balance of God's judgment.

Being surrounded by a body and living in the flesh, do not ever reject life from medical treatment. For even if you live for a long time in both well-being and health, you will not continue to be without sickness as if there were no need for the care of the healer. And having a soul inclined toward earthly things, whenever it becomes filled with the efforts of the body, do not reject mercy, so that you may not be deprived of forgiveness when you become in need of it. If someone is a priest and has been granted to lead the people, let him see the falls of those under his care with sympathy, knowing that even if the order of life differs from the many, it has not hindered the nature of those being shepherded, and that he, sharing in it, may perhaps one day share in transgression. Moses, knowing these things—for he was a man and knew human nature—commanded the calf to be used by the priest, because he was entirely a sinner and in need of cleansing and many things. What the fleshly calf was then, this is now the bodiless [sin].
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Care of the Shepherd
english: Do not let us boast and vaunt of benefits through repentance and bloodless prayer, knowing that even Aaron, the most tested priest, was drawn toward gods by the people and was caught in the murmuring along with his sister Mary; if the one who murmured had not pleaded, he would not have escaped the punishment.

Another, who is not a priest but one of many, should fear laying on a heavy yoke. For if he who is set to cleansing the people sometimes needs cleansings himself, what will happen to the one who does not even possess the power of ordination?

Let us imitate the pastoral way of the Lord; let us bow to the Gospels and, just as an image is learned in a mirror, let us learn the idea of both care and kindness. For I see there, in parables and in the shaded words, a shepherd of a hundred sheep; who, when one of the flock was torn away and went wandering, did not remain with those in order and those thought to be unerring, but having rushed to the search, pursued many bellies and ravines, and was lifted high by great and lofty obstacles and endured the wildernesses patiently, until he discovered the wanderer.

Having found him, he did not strike him, nor did he drive him back fiercely rushing toward the flock, but having laid hold of the neck and bringing him with mercy to the companions, he restored him, rejoicing more over that one than over the multitude of the others.

Let us then understand the matter that is hidden in riddles. For the sheep is not truly a sheep and the shepherd is altogether something else—not indeed a herder of mute animals—but these things are educational examples for the priests, so that regarding men we neither despair too easily nor become discouraged when they are in danger. Let us seek the one in distress and lead him back into order, and let us rejoice with those returning and mingle with the fullness of those living rightly.

It was fitting for the priest to practice philanthropy instead of excision, so that even if the Lord commands to cut off someone as a useless plant, he must ask as a gardener for mercy and for exceeding [hope]. For the word presents to us the mind of the unfruitful fig tree, where the farmer, wanting to prune it because of the unfruitfulness, pleads and asks for a regrowth and for exceeding good hopes for it.

The one who cares through his own diligence. Do not strike hastily, since you ought to prevent the one to whom the cutting was entrusted by the Lord, nor judge the uselessness quickly, but work out the diligence. Dig with reproaches, warm with exhortations like dung, water with the flowing of lessons, surround with the protective fences of commands like a trench. Let it be yours to abstain, the judge's to decide.

Let us strive to be called that, which the Lord also is called: for the Father is named Paraclete, appeasing on behalf of the human race; likewise the Spirit of Truth took the name of the zeal for us. For there also he is called Paraclete; and indeed an embassy and an intercession on behalf of the sinners is always striven for, not of the blameless and the unaccused.

Zeal, O priest, for the care of Moses; imitate his concern for those beginning their disposition, who, calling upon God, so that He might not be ill-disposed toward the people having sinned, since he knew a little that grace had passed by, this indeed he entreated: that the people might go forth, so that he might not see the destruction of the one being driven mad.

And nothing is like remembering the word of it: 'I pray, the people have sinned a great sin and have made for themselves golden gods. And now, if you forgive them their sin, let them be; but if not, blot me out from the book which you have written' (Exodus 32:32). Do you see how he sets forth the salvation of the multitude through his own care and seeks to be blotted out, if he does not succeed in obtaining forgiveness for the common [people]? But those now, being embittered toward the sinners approaching, drive them away, and those falling down, running toward, seeking to be healed, exceeding the limit, do not incline their faces while weeping.

Why then did Luke, and rather the Holy Spirit, write to me about the lost son (Luke 15), who first brought down the one just born, then, having been wasted away by pleasures and drunkenness and becoming a lover of money, emptied all the father's wealth? And since later, having been sufficiently wretched by labors, as if to become a fellow-dweller with hired hands and to share the same food with the pigs, he returned to the father's hearth having become sober, the father did not turn away nor did he shut the doors against him.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Parable of the Returning Son and the Sinful Woman
english: After his return, he approached the one drawing near and leaned on his neck, shedding tears compassionately upon the neck; and instead of an athlete's reward, he made him blessed by clothing him in free garments, putting a ring on his hand, celebrating a feast, and preparing a splendid banquet.

All these things are a parabolic word, opening to those repenting that the church is a fatherly home received with goodwill, so that they are not fellow-dwellers with swine or the filthy, but are born again as sons of another, so that by the will of God they may live together as a father's purpose and with the holy men as brothers.

You, however, do not envy the mind of the elder brother, nor grumble at the father's philanthropy, because he even received the prodigal and the insolent one. Rather marvel at the goodness and imitate God's benevolence, and embrace and fall upon those returning from error; for thus you will be a guide to the blind and a teacher of the wanderers.

Regarding those practicing harshness of mind and cutting off [mercy] before compassion, enough has been said to us and nothing more is needed; but listen also, you who pray for a return, that it might be fitting for you to hover over sins and mourn the falls of the heart. Rather, if it seems good, consider the sinful woman read to us by Luke in our presence. Zeal for her humility and modesty, and take as a rule of repentance, having remained exact.

For coming to the house of the Pharisee, she neither reddened at the crowd of those dining, nor fled the time of the banquet as unseasonable for confession, but being seized by grief and having a fierce mourning for transgressions, she did not release the physician of sins even for a moment. Nor was she coming to entreat face-to-face, but interpreting through her appearance that which was unworthy of herself and outspoken, having grasped the place by her posture and not even standing simply, but falling on her feet, loosening her hair, and making public her mourning soul through her actions, pouring tears to the feet of Jesus with much compassion, she sought mercy; and pouring out so much that she even drenched the feet, and while wringing out her hair, she gathered up all the moisture with humble reverence.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Fruitlessness of Nominal Repentance
english: It was being demonstrated. So that having gathered [the points] I might say, the woman exerted repentance through all her senses and through her habits which had sinned; and it is possible to demonstrate by inference that she was mourning her sins publicly and in an obvious way, whereas she used to practice [sin] privately in her leisure. As for us, our promise announces repentance, but our practice shows nothing additional, but rather we maintain the same state of life which we lived even before the sin.

For brightness is the same, and the same clothing, and a luxurious enjoyment of the table, and long sleep relaxed into indolence, and various distractions and cares producing forgetfulness to the soul through its own self-care. But we are only inscribed with the name of repentance, being both unfruitful and inactive; separating ourselves from the mysteries and from the communion of the secret sanctifications, and making no effort at all for a return toward them, but rather despising the enjoyment as if it were easy.

Understand, man, that you are worthy of many things, yet you have been separated from the participation of those. If you were a participant at a royal table, and then, having struck against the honor, you were cast off, how much wealth would you spend to become a friend and table-fellow again? And what doors would you not have pursued, begging, being at a loss, groaning, considering life unlivable, manifesting the pain of the grief in the depths through rank and relation of person, moving every stone, even the stone of the word, until you had overcome the calamity for yourself?

But he who, having been separated from the intimacy toward God and having fallen from truly high honor, what great and significant thing of a corrupted soul will he demonstrate of humility? It is not consistent to say that one who is sick is changing to the same life as those who are healthy. For a different diet is for the sick one, and a different life for the healthy one.

See how great is the change of the well-off toward the condition of the ailing; for he, sensing the illness according to its state, lies down in a small room, having withdrawn from all habit, neglecting agriculture, being a very farmer, and abandoning concern for wealth...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Physician of the Soul
english: A speculator and a lover of money. He is nourished by water and pulse, even if formerly he was full of luxury and set a Sybaritic table. Separated from his usual marriage-bed, he does not delight children; he understands doctors both by night and by day, and for the sake of beloved profit, he hastens toward health with many wages. Such is the sick man of the body.

But he who is badly disposed regarding the soul, having surrounded the incorporeal [soul] with [physical] ailments, and feigning confession and showing weakness, leaves [it] to be devoured and torn apart by the passion, so that it might be spread out over the whole mass? But be temperate, know yourself: you have grieved God, having insulted your Creator, who has authority over this present life and is Lord and Judge of the life to come. Have you been harmed by luxury? Through fasting, heal the enjoyment. Has intemperance harmed the soul? Let temperance become the medicine for the sickness.

Has greed worked a many-layered fever upon the intellect? Let almsgiving empty the fullness, for it is the distribution of cleansing for those who have been filled. Has the seizing of others' things harmed us? Let the stolen thing return to its own master. Falsehood has brought us near to destruction; for he says, 'You shall perish, those who speak falsehood' (John 8:44); let studied truth stand against the danger.

A broken oath leads to the flying sickle of Zechariah threatening to cut the womb (Zech 9:1); let us put on the whole armor of repentance, so that we might repel the edge of the sickle. Has someone served impiously through heretical dogmas? Let him drive away superstition with the mindset of right belief. This indeed is repentance: a release and an undoing of those [things] formerly or according to practice being enacted, or according to disposition being thought.

But he who knows the usefulness of the seventy [times] of repentance, yet is always turning toward the filth of lawlessness, becomes a slave alongside one who knows the wrath of the master, yet in his presence works evil and triples the sin. Let him become sensitive toward the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Physician of the Soul
english: [It is] containing a disease. Crush yourself as much as you can; seek also the mourning of like-souled brothers to help you toward freedom. Show me your bitter and abundant tear, so that I may mix mine as well; take also the priest, a fellow-mourner of the affliction, as a father.

For who is such a false father or one adamant regarding the soul, as not to journey with the grieving children or to rejoice with them again? A priest is a son of [God] according to religion; he mourns sin just as Jacob [mourned] for Joseph's blood-stained tunic (Gen 37:31), as David [mourned] for Absalom's destruction, as Eli [mourned] for Hophni and Phinehas falling in the battle line, as Moses [mourned] for the people who innovated the godless calf-making (Ex 32).

Be emboldened before the [One] who begot you according to God, before the bodily fathers; show Him unashamedly the hidden things, strip bare the soul's secrets as one showing a hidden disease to a physician; He himself will attend to both decency and the cure; for the shame of parents touches those whom they have suffered. For the glory of those who begot is likewise their shame. The term of life is uncertain, brothers. Let us outpace the departure through care.

For it is absurd that those who calculate their providence according to the flesh cleanse themselves from material things before the circumcision of the so-called dog, lest the moisture that causes disease should work rot through excessive heat; but those who need care according to the intellect do not outrun the uncertainty of death and the heat of the testing fire, which burns unbidden and is never quenched.

You had the evangelical drachma and were enriching yourself well with the money, then through laziness you lost it. Light the lamp of repentance (Matt 25:1), bow down with care, seek the treasure hidden to the poor through afflictions (Matt 13:44). Having found it, lift it up and save it, so that we neighbors may rejoice with you in the joy in Christ, to whom glory is due, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Benefits of Fasting for Soul and Body
english: Man is a composite being, consisting of a visible body and a rational and incorporeal soul.

Of these two previously mentioned things, the nature and the value are not equal; for the one [the body] was created as an instrument to move according to the economy of the ruling [soul], but the other was appointed to rule and to reign as superior to the inferior.

Having received discernment from the intellect and the logos, and finding the difference between the good and the not-such, it [the soul] recognizes God as Creator and Maker of the things in these senses, and not only these, but also of the invisible things, which the incorporeal mind, through imagination, sees.

Practicing justice and virtue as a friend of God, it [the soul] pursues philosophy and, obeying its laws and commands, leads itself to something greater than the fleshly desires, and draws near to God with whatever power belongs to the good.

The most important and predominant part of this holy philosophy turns toward what is called self-control; for from this point the mind remains unpolluted, receiving no mixture of the filths from the stomach or of other impurities, and it has unhindered activity and the contemplation of heavenly and kindred things.

Therefore, you who are nourished by philosophy, lovers of the high things, and disciples of the Word, love this present time and the holy forty days; receive it as a teacher of temperance and a mother of virtue, a nourisher of the sons of God, a pedagogue of the unruly, a calm of souls, a stability of life, and a peace that is both a pledge and undisturbed.
For this strict and solemn passion puts to sleep the impulses and the tempers, and it cools and restrains all the turbulence sought by gluttony. And just as in the summer, when the sun...

Just as the north wind benefits the things being warmed by the glowing lamp of the earth, driving away the suffocation with gentle breezes, so also fasting grants benefit, having driven away the burning of the bodies from gluttony.

Doing so much for the soul, it benefits the body no less. For it thins the thicknesses and the bulk of the material elements, it unloads the weight of the body, and it brings down the veins bursting from the abundance of blood and gives a little room to the narrowness, so that they may not suffer the passion of the vessels. For even those, when much and immoderate water is held back beyond the capacity, they burst from the volume being forced in by violence, not containing it.

And it has a gentle head and one stilled in its posture, neither the arteries throbbing nor the brain being darkened by the rising of vapors. And of the stomach, self-control is freedom. For then it is released from the necessary slavery and from boiling like a cauldron, exhausting the entrails. Eyes see clearly and without scrutiny, all the film being removed, which the boy is accustomed to pouring over the eyes, and the base of the feet is firm, and the activity of the hands is unshakeable.

Breath is orderly and moderate, by none of the spirits that crowd from within rushing forth. The word of the faster is clear and well-structured, the mind is pure and then truly possesses the god-like, when as in an incorporeal state it performs its own activity in the flesh, painless and without disturbance. Sleeps are painless and without phantasms; and so that I may say many things by passing over much, fasting is a common peace of soul and body, an undisturbed life, a stable constitution, a life pleasing to God and grieving the enemy.

For just as the enemy, when he sees the opponent alert and sober, arming himself with care and practicing courage, considers his love of battle to be a lesser thing, so also the attacker of our salvation considers all our precision according to virtue as a threat to himself.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The corruption of lineages through appetite
english: He hates misfortune. And because of this, it comes to pass that the house of the fasting person has angels as guardians, protectors, and attendants, while the one indulging in pleasures during the forty days has demons as household members, and lovers and lustful ones of blood, and attendants of drunkenness. For even regarding the spirits, whether holy or unclean, each one approaches its own kind and friends, just as it can be seen among birds.

For a dove indeed loves the pure places and turns itself toward the clearings, sowing seed for itself and its young; and the berry sits sweetly upon the tree leaves, producing something sweet and thin. But the gluttonous raven sits near the butcher shops, heavy and unpleasant, descending upon those who are slaughtering meat.

Therefore, let us love self-control, so that we may be loved by angels, and let us hate unrestrained luxury, so that we may not cast ourselves into fellowship with demons along with it. No one living in luxury became diligent, nor is one idling in prayers a disciple of virtue, nor is a lover of pleasure a saint, nor is one living fleshly a companion of the kingdom.

Come into your memory toward the beginning of our race and you will find the experience of those of whom we are witnesses. For a law of fasting would not have been set for us if the law of first self-control had not been surpassed; nor would the stomach have been named an intruder, if the pretext of pleasure had not introduced sin.

There was no need for the plow, nor for oxen to plow, nor for the cutting of the furrow, nor indeed for the sowing of seed and the watering, nor for the cycle of seasons, nor for the thickening of winter and the loosening of summer, nor for all this cyclical toil, if we had not decided upon the cycle of labors for the sake of an easy, immediate enjoyment of this [life]; but we intended a different state of life from the one seen, which we again hope to attain when we put on the impassible life through the resurrection.

For this is the blessing of God's condescension toward us, so that we might restore our worth toward the former [state]; which, having taken hold of philanthropically, we did not preserve, feeling the grace sensitively. Let us therefore be brightened at the coming fast; an icon of the coming life, a mimic of the incorruptible conduct. There are neither drinking parties nor pleasures...

Leave the first man, and count those after him as well. Why did it make the righteous Noah act shamefully, being stripped of his members which law should cover, and prepare to mock the impious Ham through the drunkenness of his father (Gen 9:20-27), so that two evils might come from one fault? For one drunkenness stripped both the father of the good covering and the son of liberty.

But when I turn again to the children of Eli the priest and to that history (1 Sam 2), I find a cluster of misfortunes connected to one another from a single source, that of the belly and the penis. For they, having made the priesthood of the father a starting point for pleasure and enjoyment, defiled the sacrifices and went toward the belly before God of the priests. And fornication followed, the sister of the sin of luxury, and to all these, the judgment from God brings a strict and sudden sentence.

For an enemy nation marched against Jerusalem because of them. And so that the word might cut short a multitude of gloomy narratives, the unrestrained youths fell in battle, the mother endangered with the sinners, and the ark of God was taken captive by the enemies, and the old priest died at the messages of evils, and so much of our evil was brought upon the city through the pleasure of the throat.

Therefore, let us all fast; especially those who are members of the priests, and more so as having the teaching of self-control and the philosophical commands from the table as a co-dweller. For it is absurd for the children of money-changers to be silver-knowers, and the members of the coppersmiths to be near the fire and the bellows, but for the members of the priests, whether relatives or otherwise, to neglect the object of life which the master and lord of the hearth was permitted to live. He was most harmed through the belly, even the elder son of Isaac (Gen 25). For being a hunter by profession and once, after a great run to the house, returning hungry, he took in the food that was before him, and he gave the firstborns to the lentil-eater (Gen 25:30-34); from there, moreover, he also snatched away the paternal blessing, and thus, being made a stranger little by little, he lost virtue and the patriarchal glory of God.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Soul and the Body
english: He lost even Israel through their lifestyle, becoming himself a barbarian and a stranger, and begetting a people like him. This disease led even the people of the old covenant into transgression of the divine and holy laws. For while Moses was occupied with the leisure of the giving of the law, the people, being distracted, turned toward luxury and dancing; the devil dragged them, as they were slipping and trampling the order of life toward impiety. From there, the demon-possessed skill of calf-making, Aaron sharing in the defilement and the corruption of the law, the smashing of the tablets, and Moses' second ascent to the mountain—all these things, which the history mocks with full detail, had their beginning and cause in immoderate eating.

I wish to set before you another account, second in time to what was said before, but equal in practice. King Saul was preparing and leading the war with much care; he forbade the people to take food on that day, sealing the judgment with an oath, and death was the penalty to the one who disobeyed. But while the whole army obediently received the command, only the king's son Jonathan stumbled, being overcome by the honey, and he dared to taste the scepter of sweetness by rushing toward the lords. Danger came near, unless the whole multitude, acting in concert with the impulse of their father and king, decided to turn the threat into action.

Regarding what has been said, it is possible to collect ten thousand such things from the Scriptures to see clearly that self-control is good, and conversely, the unrestrained enjoyment of drink and food is harmful. Fasting is the companion of the saints; fasting is the leader of every good work. And just as craftsmen do not perform their arts without tools, so also the diligent, even when helping with spiritual gifts, have never performed any of the wonders and marvels without self-control. Fasting Elijah raised the dead and gave them life; fasting Moses saw God; fasting Daniel mastered the sorcery and error of the Assyrians; fasting the Lord withstood the temptations of the devil; and fasting the...

The apostles performed prayers for important matters; the Ninevites through fasting overcame the threat of death (Jonah 3:5-10). This [prayer] is an intercessor toward God, worthy of reverence, and a reliable embassy that quickly covers itself with shame for whatever supplication it brings to God.

Therefore, let every pious man, who loves God more than pleasure, approach the days of self-control with joy and good cheer. For no one who is merely a scavenger is a noble combatant at the beginning of the contests.

Do not become sullen like a child being dragged to school; do not grumble about the purity of the days; do not seek the end of the week like the arrival of spring after a bitter winter; do not long for the Sabbath for the sake of feasting like a Jew (Exodus 16); do not count the days of the forty [days] like a lazy laborer waiting for the end of his agreed-upon wage; do not grieve because from the first hour your house is not smoking, nor has the cook stood by the fire.

Grant something also to the soul, not everything to the body. The former nourishes by the withholding of food, the latter by the abundance. But since the two are joined to one another, and those which are much separated by nature are seated together by the providence and art of the Creator, let us deliberate so that both might happen, each not being deprived of what is appropriate. You, O man, were composed of the two, and I am entirely silent as to the fact that the soul is much more preferable and it was fitting that it should receive the greater share of favor.

But judge between both as a rational and discerning man. Consider a little, and if you wish, I will make the argument for the soul as if to a faithful woman, providing support regarding those things of which she says she is being treated unjustly and being cast down. This, then, is sacred and incorporeal, immortal and incorruptible, having its kinship not toward earth and these things, but toward God. Being pure, she rejoices with the pure, and having an incorporeal origin, she flees from material substances.

However, since the vessel formed from the earth was commanded to be managed, as an obedient handmaid to the Lord, she sits upon the clay and is subject to the guarding and the providence over it, until the command comes allowing the separation. This [abstinence] from food, which gives life to the body, is necessary; but for the organ of the earth, the enjoyment of food is necessary. He seeks nothing...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Virtue of Temperance and the Example of Barbarians
english: Even more as a superior. 14.9.4 'Divide to me, he says, the time of the year; give the six months for enjoyment to the one being governed and the remaining to the governor.' The request is just, and no judge is so fond of wisdom, being a heterodox judge, as not to vote in favor of those things being said. 14.10.1 But I will even do an excess; I do not hold to equality. I descend with the weakness of the body. I leave ten months to the body and a little more. Let the fortieth be granted to me, unpolluted, so that I might be slightly freed from the filth, the mud, having been cooled by self-control. These things, O Christians, are both just and irrefutable, even if God judges and even if man judges. 14.10.2 And you also, O judge, vote in my favor, for the time has arrived when the soul is disputing against the body. Therefore, take away from me, O Christian, the sensuality as if it were childish. You are a man; do not think the things of infants. If he does not receive that of honey, he wails; if you do not crave meat or wine, he falls away, tears himself apart, and knocks down everyone for more, while lamenting. 14.10.3 I redden at the descent of the gluttons, so that they might mourn the fasting; they are constantly gaping, they are slightly overcome, they pass away again, they sleep by necessity. In insensibility they strive to pass the days, they are weary of the sun toward the setting as it grows late. They approach the days as longer than the habit. Moreover, they wash their aching stomachs and the tensions of the spirits and the heaviness of the head and the dizziness of the state. 14.10.4 Even if these things are of surfeit, they are not the characteristics of fasting. They come to the solemn table joylessly, they grumble about the vegetables, they revile the legumes as if they were an addition added to creation; for the lovers of pleasure become also blowhards against the appearances of self-control. 14.10.5 They draw water without breath as if they had received a tasteless medicine from physicians to drink. And many also act wise regarding wine, persuading their pleasure with illicit concoctions. And others immediately attend to the need for vegetables and become various sophists of enjoyment. But this is very habitual and senseless. 14.10.6 For self-control is a struggle of the self-governing and of the free mind, m—
The text ends abruptly with a fragment: 'μ' (m—).

For a slave-like craft, seeking what is set before it, does not work it as it should, but fashions it in a slavish way. You demand a reward for those things according to which you live by the law of virtue. But a reward is promised to honest workers, not to evildoers.

Do not corrupt the fast, so that you do not suffer the things of the charcoal-burners. For if those, mixing water with wine, are punished, how will you, by introducing your sophisticated pleasures into the strictness of the fast, pass through unpunished? Do not imitate formed weaknesses; do not deceive yourself regarding the forty days as if it were a disease-maker, for on the contrary, it is a maker of health. Do not make pretexts for sins while working with men driven by lust.

Because of bad habit, self-control is considered an enemy to you; it is not, however, naturally offensive. All barbarians are a proof of this word, those who neither plant vines nor drink wine, but instead take for themselves by habit an uncultivated drink, water, and they are known to be brave and excellent in wars and they hold sway over the many, as is fitting, those who are drunk while they are sober.

But bodies to them are light and vigorous, and such people are quick to mount a horse, and are skillful and bold and accurate toward archery. And they are capable of finding safety amidst the tumult and finding a course in destitute places. Therefore, do not accuse water as being an emollient, and do not say that those using it are weak; for experience will expose your slander.

What do I say about wine? The Scythian nomads, those who dwell by the Bosporus and those who are stationed by the Rhine river, are indeed homeless and unstanding. But they live from skins and hides and from the hanging veils, making for themselves a covering.

But they do not know a plow, nor do they turn the soil; therefore they also do not bring bread. For how could those who have not learned agriculture regarding grain and the subsequent seeds be expected to? Nevertheless, living without bread and wine, they are brave and worthy of fighting war against all nations, and they hold sway over and excel the many; and neither bread nor wine being absent from them harmed them, but the ancestral habit became nature to men.
Why then did the word mention these things? In order that...

title: The Discipline of Self-Control
english: Let us learn how training and discipline shape a person toward whatever we desire and meditate upon. Habituate yourself to self-control, and in time it will become an unforced, constant companion to you. But if, on the contrary, you have companions and friends for your pleasures and banquets, you will never love fasting; instead, it will appear to you as heavy as a stranger or something unusual.

14.12.2 A self-controlled life is an icon of the coming and incorruptible life. For just as when we stripped off this passion-filled flesh, we shall live freely, having no necessity to serve the stomach and no slavery to other passions, so also if we now cast off the great necessity and matter of ourselves, we shall be near the expected incorruption. To speak briefly: let us flee from love of pleasure toward strength; for it is impossible to be both a lover of pleasure and a lover of God.

14.12.3 For the lover of wisdom will be, by necessity, also a lover of money, and the lover of money will be unjust; and he who has fallen into injustice will easily transgress the laws of piety and trample the rules of the wise, and will easily lay hands on what is forbidden, thereby gathering for himself the materials of pleasure and offering all the spoils of injustice to hedonism as to a mistress.

14.12.4 Do not flee from the hardship of self-control, but set hopes against the present toil, and when the lightness of the reward has passed by, avoid the abstention. Say to yourself words of piety: Fasting is bitter, but paradise is sweet; thirst is heavy, but near is the spring from which the drinker will never thirst for all eternity. The body is frail, but the soul, which is without a body, is stronger. Power is dead, but near is the resurrection.

14.12.5 Say to your approaching stomach and to yourself the word of the Lord: 'Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God' (Matt 4:4). It is not a famine, but a small temptation; it is not a necessary punishment, but a voluntary abstention; it is not a slavery-like necessity, but a free philosophy. Pray and you will be strong; call upon Him, and the Helper stands ready for you.

14.13.1 Take up in your memory an ancient history and learn how those who, through piety, press down the body, compared to those living in luxury and pouring out much of the unmixed [wine], are neither weaker in strength, nor are they more gloomy or having lost their grace.

14.13.2 For that King of the Assyrians, who lived entirely in the flesh and was bound to a luxurious life like a glutton, commanded his cupbearers and cooks and all the simple servants of pleasure to be chosen for their intelligence and to appear graceful, so that not only the mouth and taste, but also his eye might enjoy through what was seen; then indeed the three youths, having been selected from the captivity of Israel according to the roster of the servants, abstaining from the sight of the king...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Beauty of Fasting and the Example of Samson
english: Because the table was defiled by the mixing with those sacrificing to idols, they ate only seeds. There was also wine poured out for the libation and all meat because of the previously stated reason.

As they were forced by the one presiding to partake in what was being offered to them, lest perhaps their beauty be changed into deformity from self-restraint, and thus that person's reproach and punishment might become the unsightly and unhealed state of the youths; 'Spare us,' they say, 'so that we may not appear less honorable to the King of the revelers, nor shall our faces be rejected, nor will you approach as if presenting to him deformed servants.' For the Artisan of our formation will give grace and will teach through experience, that God is the caretaker of our beauty and fasting is the attendant of the sought-after elegance. And that which has indeed happened. For the youths exceeded all and they all emboldened the meat-eaters.

And what of Samson? Immediately from milk he was not taught to fast in such a way as it was fitting for the child, having been suckled by his mother, to abstain from wine and to guard against all luxury? And who was strong like him? And who was the left-handed one so famously named? He alone was a worthy combatant against every arrangement of wars, and an innumerable multitude he turned back by power; he who, having lacked sword or spear, but ascending upon the jawbone of a donkey, destroyed warlike men by using only the bone.

So then also you were hoping and you shall be strong; with readiness and with power you shall become; give ear to the learning of the hidden things and forget food, just as the people following Jesus, being instructed in word and deed. Let us, the incontinent and the pleasure-loving, Greeks and Jews, not fast in vain and for no end; for they are vainly penalized for what they do not eat, except as a zeal for the matter, which is fitting for the serious.

For Christians, precision in conduct and dignity in philosophy are proper, to whom the pure and true word of piety is present. But those who practice moral discipline apart from this seem to me to be working like those building a house without a foundation or launching a ship without it being steered. Such Hebrews are ill-known. And laughter falls heavily upon me when I behold them, unendurable, wandering around the white mortars with amphorae, a mockery of Moses, a shame to the prophets.

title: The Misunderstanding of Types and the Purpose of Fasting
english: The offspring of Abraham are abortions, slaves of thoughtlessness instead of sons of freedom, ignorant and lawless though supposedly disciples of the law, having lost the hope of the outcome because they did not rationally receive the types of what is to come.

For Moses, in everything he did, prefigured the idols that would come later; whether you speak of the fast, or the feast of tabernacles, or the sounding of the trumpets, likewise the circumcision, the unleavened bread, the bitter herbs. All those things were messages and icons pre-drawn for those being initiated into the mysteries toward the completion.

For I, the Christian, fast well as a slave of the crucified, whether purifying myself toward the hope of the resurrection or clinging as a devoted slave to the sufferings of my Lord. But you, son of the murderers and descendant of those who slaughtered the lamb, having received the inheritance of the shed blood through the voice of the fathers, who thus made vows for themselves and their children, tell me, for what purpose do you fast? If it is as one repenting of the things in which you sinned—I support you in this opinion—and leaving the assembly of those committing adultery, hasten toward the church of the pious. Come to the blood of the lamb and be sprinkled; for from there purification for you shall exist, from which I shall stand away from sin. But if you are still bound to the same things, what do you intend by the abstention from food, or are you imitating the Nile crocodiles, whom they say roar at the heads of the men they ate and weep for the slaughter, not taking repentance for what happened, but rather the fleshless, it seems to me, mourning the head as if it were unfit for eating? Such also is the form regarding the fast.

The fasts are mere dances and plays, middle parts and episodes, things fighting against the outward appearance; for fasting is understood as a pedagogue of thickening and the restraint of elegance, while the dance interprets the spilled [liquid] with unbridled and many pleasantries.

For remember here the Mosaic word saying to fast on the tenth of the seventh month. For the seventh month denotes the seventh day, and the tenth denotes the tenth hour, in which the Lord on the cross gave up [the ghost].

title: The Typology of Festivals and the Trumpet
english: The Spirit distinguishes each thing, and the forms of sensible appearance reveal the invisible disposition of the soul. Why do you mix the unmixed and carry together those things which are separated? There are other common festivals for them. One they call the Feast of Tabernacles, and another I hear is the remembrance of trumpets. But they celebrate the mysteries of Christians in ignorance, because the creation of the Tabernacle is the practical prophecy of this Church, which our Word established.

For this reason, they also adorn the Tabernacle with leaves and beautify the courts with flowers, as a type of how the new Church is to bring forth fruitfulness by the law. But the feast of the trumpets rouses the souls toward the preparation for the resurrection, as Paul says: 'For the dead shall also be sounded forth and shall arise' (1 Cor 15:52). And God our Savior also teaches in the Gospels, saying: 'And he will send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they will gather his elect from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other' (Matt 24:31).

Hearing these words, they will perhaps use such a contradiction against us: that, remembering the ancient wonders and the blessings of God, they bring these thanksgivings forward in favor of Mount Sinai and the trumpet that sounded at the giving of the law. But the thoughtless will not know that even then the trumpet was taken as a type during the giving of the law.

Since he who receives the law for a rule of life and an orderly polity must demonstrate the punishment for disobedience, therefore God, sending the written commands of our life to men, immediately added also the voice of the trumpet, a symbol of the resurrection from the dead, so that the disciples of the commands, foreseeing the judgment through the resurrection, might guard the doctrines as safeguards of the divine legislation.

Do not fasting and the Feast of Tabernacles and the trumpets of our piety also constitute mysteries of our piety, once indicated in shadow, but reaching their outcome in the proper time, when the theophanies in the flesh of our Savior were completed; to whom belongs the glory and the honor and the worship, now and forever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.
